steps: Step 1, Meet three letters and the three short vowels. The letter ب is read b: بَ (ba, with fatha, a small slash above), بِ (bi, with kasra, a small slash below), بُ (bu, with damma, a small curl above). Say each sound aloud three times.

Step 2, Do the same with ت and ا. تَ (ta), تِ (ti), تُ (tu). The letter ا (alif) carries the vowel sound: أَ (a), إِ (i), أُ (u). Read this row slowly, pointing at each mark: بَ تَ أَ، بِ تِ إِ، بُ تُ أُ.

Step 3, Join letters into real words. بَاب [door] has the long vowel alif. بِنْت [girl] and تَمْر [dates] show the little circle called sukun (ْ), which means no vowel on that letter. Sound them out: ba-b, bin-t, tam-r.

Step 4, Practise a tiny question and answer. Teacher: مَا هَذَا؟ [What is this?] Child: هَذَا بَاب. [This is a door.] Teacher: وَمَا هَذَا؟ [And what is this?] Child: هَذَا تَمْر. [These are dates.] Point at pictures as you ask and answer.

Step 5, Spot the common error. A learner reads بِ as ba, ignoring the kasra under the letter. Correction: a mark below means i, so بِ is bi. Another error is writing بَاب as three separate letters ب ا ب; in a word the letters join from right to left.

Step 6, Your turn: read these aloud, then write the word for house. تُ، تِ، بَ، بُ. Model answer: tu, ti, ba, bu. The word for house is بَيْت [house], read bayt; check you wrote ب first on the right, then ي, then ت.

Step 1, Learn the first greeting pair. One child says السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ [Peace be upon you] and the other answers وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ [And upon you peace]. Say it with a smile and a small nod. Also learn the simple hello: مَرْحَبًا [Hello].

Step 2, Learn the time-of-day greetings. صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ [Good morning] is answered with صَبَاحُ النُّورِ [Morning of light]. In the evening say مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ [Good evening], answered with مَسَاءُ النُّورِ. Practise both pairs with a partner.

Step 3, Add polite words. شُكْرًا [Thank you] is answered with عَفْوًا [You're welcome]. To ask for something say مِنْ فَضْلِكَ [please, to a boy]. At the end of the lesson say مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ [Goodbye]. Say each one while handing a pencil to your partner.

Step 4, Act out a short dialogue. A: مَرْحَبًا! كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ [Hello! How are you?] B: أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ، شُكْرًا. [I am well, thank you.] A: عَفْوًا. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ. [You're welcome. Goodbye.] B: مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ. [Goodbye.]

Step 5, Fix a common error. A boy says to a girl: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. Correction: for a girl the ending changes, so say مِنْ فَضْلِكِ [please, to a girl]. Likewise كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟ [How are you? to a girl] is used for a girl and حَالُكَ for a boy.

Step 6, Your turn: say good morning to your teacher, thank a friend for a pencil, then say goodbye. Model answer: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ [Good morning]. شُكْرًا [Thank you]. عَفْوًا [You're welcome]. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ [Goodbye].

Step 1, Learn the family words with my: أَبِي [my father], أُمِّي [my mother], أَخِي [my brother], أُخْتِي [my sister], جَدِّي [my grandfather], جَدَّتِي [my grandmother]. The ending ـي means my. Say each word while pointing at a family photo.

Step 2, Name people with هَذَا for a male and هَذِهِ for a female. هَذَا أَبِي. [This is my father.] هَذَا أَخِي. [This is my brother.] هَذِهِ أُمِّي. [This is my mother.] هَذِهِ أُخْتِي. [This is my sister.] Read each pair twice.

Step 3, Learn the rooms. غُرْفَةُ النَّوْمِ [bedroom], الْمَطْبَخُ [kitchen], الْحَمَّامُ [bathroom], غُرْفَةُ الْجُلُوسِ [sitting room]. Say: هَذِهِ غُرْفَةُ النَّوْمِ. [This is the bedroom.] غُرْفَةٌ is feminine, so it takes هَذِهِ.

Step 4, Practise a mini dialogue. A: أَيْنَ أُمِّي؟ [Where is my mother?] B: هِيَ فِي الْمَطْبَخِ. [She is in the kitchen.] A: وَأَيْنَ أَبِي؟ [And where is my father?] B: هُوَ فِي غُرْفَةِ الْجُلُوسِ. [He is in the sitting room.]

Step 5, Correct a typical mistake. A child says هَذَا أُمِّي. Correction: أُمِّي is feminine, so say هَذِهِ أُمِّي [This is my mother]. Remember the pairs: هَذَا with أَبِي and أَخِي, هَذِهِ with أُمِّي and أُخْتِي.

Step 6, Your turn: introduce your grandmother and say she is in the kitchen. Model answer: هَذِهِ جَدَّتِي. هِيَ فِي الْمَطْبَخِ. [This is my grandmother. She is in the kitchen.] Then point to a room and name it.

Step 1, Learn six colours: أَحْمَرُ [red], أَزْرَقُ [blue], أَخْضَرُ [green], أَصْفَرُ [yellow], أَبْيَضُ [white], أَسْوَدُ [black]. Hold up crayons and say each name. These are the forms for a masculine thing, such as حِصَانٌ أَسْوَدُ [a black horse].

Step 2, Count to ten: وَاحِد، اثْنَان، ثَلَاثَة، أَرْبَعَة، خَمْسَة، سِتَّة، سَبْعَة، ثَمَانِيَة، تِسْعَة، عَشَرَة [one to ten]. Clap once for each number as you say it, then count ten fingers from right to left.

Step 3, Name animals: قِطَّة [cat], كَلْب [dog], حِصَان [horse], عُصْفُور [bird], سَمَكَة [fish]. Make a sentence: عِنْدِي قِطَّةٌ بَيْضَاءُ. [I have a white cat.] For a feminine animal the colour changes to بَيْضَاءُ [white, feminine].

Step 4, Combine numbers and animals. هُنَا كَلْبٌ وَاحِدٌ وَقِطَّتَانِ. [Here are one dog and two cats.] The ending ـتَانِ means two of something feminine. Ask: مَا لَوْنُ الْحِصَانِ؟ [What colour is the horse?] Answer: أَسْوَدُ. [Black.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says قِطَّةٌ أَبْيَضُ. Correction: قِطَّةٌ بَيْضَاءُ, because قِطَّة is feminine and needs the feminine colour. For a masculine word keep أَبْيَضُ: كَلْبٌ أَبْيَضُ [a white dog].

Step 6, Your turn: say you have a green bird and three fish. Model answer: عِنْدِي عُصْفُورٌ أَخْضَرُ [I have a green bird] وَثَلَاثُ سَمَكَاتٍ [and three fish]. Then count the animals in a picture aloud from one to ten.

Step 1, Say hello and your name. Bonjour ! [Hello!] Je m'appelle Léa. [My name is Léa.] Replace Léa with your own name. Use Salut ! [Hi!] with friends and Bonjour with teachers. Practise standing up and saying it clearly.

Step 2, Ask and answer about age and feelings. Tu as quel âge ? [How old are you?] J'ai six ans. [I am six years old.] Ça va ? [How are you?] Ça va bien, merci. [I am fine, thank you.] Note J'ai, not Je suis, for age.

Step 3, Act out a first meeting. Léa : Bonjour ! Comment tu t'appelles ? [Hello! What is your name?] Hugo : Je m'appelle Hugo. Et toi ? [My name is Hugo. And you?] Léa : Enchantée, Hugo ! [Nice to meet you, Hugo!] Hugo : Enchanté, Léa ! [Nice to meet you, Léa!]

Step 4, Say goodbye politely. Au revoir ! [Goodbye!] À demain ! [See you tomorrow!] Merci, madame. [Thank you, madam.] S'il vous plaît. [Please.] Say each phrase with the right gesture: wave for au revoir and nod for merci.

Step 5, Fix a common error. A child says Je suis appelle Léa. Correction: Je m'appelle Léa, never je suis appelle. Another slip is Je suis six ans; say J'ai six ans, because French says I have six years.

Step 6, Your turn: introduce yourself with name, age and a goodbye. Model answer: Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Karim. J'ai sept ans. Ça va bien, merci. Au revoir ! [Hello! My name is Karim. I am seven. I am fine, thank you. Goodbye!]

Step 1, Count from one to ten: un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, dix. Say them with your fingers. The final x of deux and dix is silent, and the t of huit is pronounced. Repeat three times, getting faster.

Step 2, Learn colours: rouge [red], bleu [blue], jaune [yellow], vert [green], noir [black], blanc [white]. Hold up coloured objects and ask: C'est de quelle couleur ? [What colour is it?] Answer: C'est rouge. [It is red.]

Step 3, Put numbers and things together. J'ai trois crayons. [I have three pencils.] J'ai deux balles rouges. [I have two red balls.] Combien de pommes ? [How many apples?] Cinq pommes. [Five apples.] Practise with real objects on your desk.

Step 4, Dialogue with a friend. Tom : Quelle est ta couleur préférée ? [What is your favourite colour?] Sara : Ma couleur préférée est le bleu. [My favourite colour is blue.] Tom : Moi, j'aime le vert. [I like green.] Sara : Super ! [Great!]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says un balle. Correction: une balle, because balle is feminine. Say un crayon but une gomme. With colours, many add an e for feminine: une pomme verte [a green apple], une chaise blanche [a white chair].

Step 6, Your turn: say you have four yellow pencils and one blue ball. Model answer: J'ai quatre crayons jaunes et une balle bleue. [I have four yellow pencils and a blue ball.] Then ask a friend: Combien de crayons ? [How many pencils?]

Step 1, Learn fruit names with articles. la pomme [the apple], la banane [the banana], la fraise [the strawberry], l'orange [the orange], le raisin [the grapes]. Note that l' is used before a vowel. Say them while looking at pictures.

Step 2, Learn food words: le pain [bread], le lait [milk], le fromage [cheese], l'eau [water], le gâteau [cake]. Ask: Qu'est-ce que c'est ? [What is it?] Answer: C'est du pain. [It is some bread.] Practise with picture cards.

Step 3, Say what you like. J'aime les bananes. [I like bananas.] J'aime les fraises. [I like strawberries.] Je n'aime pas le fromage. [I do not like cheese.] Use les for plural fruit you like in general.

Step 4, Order at the table. Maman : Tu as faim ? [Are you hungry?] Lucas : Oui, j'ai faim ! [Yes, I am hungry!] Maman : Tu veux une pomme ? [Do you want an apple?] Lucas : Oui, merci. Je voudrais aussi de l'eau, s'il te plaît. [Yes, thank you. I would also like some water, please.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says J'aime le bananes. Correction: J'aime les bananes, because the noun is plural and needs les. Another error is une lait; say du lait or le lait, because lait is masculine.

Step 6, Your turn: say you like strawberries and do not like cheese, then ask for bread politely. Model answer: J'aime les fraises. Je n'aime pas le fromage. Je voudrais du pain, s'il vous plaît. [I like strawberries. I do not like cheese. I would like some bread, please.]
Step 1, Say the seven days in order: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. Notice that French days begin with a small letter. Chant them like a song, clapping on each syllable.

Step 2, Say the twelve months: janvier, février, mars, avril, mai, juin, juillet, août, septembre, octobre, novembre, décembre. Months also use small letters. Say them in groups of four, then all twelve without stopping.

Step 3, Ask and answer. Quel jour est-ce aujourd'hui ? [What day is it today?] Aujourd'hui, c'est mardi. [Today it is Tuesday.] Demain, c'est mercredi. [Tomorrow it is Wednesday.] Hier, c'était lundi. [Yesterday it was Monday.] Use a classroom calendar.

Step 4, Talk about birthdays. Quand est ton anniversaire ? [When is your birthday?] Mon anniversaire est en mars. [My birthday is in March.] Mon anniversaire est le dix mai. [My birthday is on the tenth of May.] Ask three classmates and note their months.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes Lundi, Mardi with capital letters, as in English. Correction: lundi, mardi. Another slip is dimanche sounding like dee-manch with a hard English sound; keep the soft French sound of ch.

Step 6, Your turn: say today's day, tomorrow's day and your birthday month. Model answer: Aujourd'hui, c'est jeudi. Demain, c'est vendredi. Mon anniversaire est en octobre. [Today is Thursday. Tomorrow is Friday. My birthday is in October.]
Step 1, Say the first vowels: अ आ इ ई उ ऊ ए ऐ ओ औ. Say each sound slowly: a, aa, i, ee, u, oo, e, ai, o, au. Trace each letter in the air with your finger, and write the top line (shirorekha) first.
Step 2, Link vowels to words. अ से अनार [A for pomegranate], आ से आम [Aa for mango], इ से इमली [I for tamarind], उ से उल्लू [U for owl]. Say the full line each time, like a chant: अ से अनार।

Step 3, Say the first consonants: क ख ग घ. क से कमल [K for lotus], ख से खरगोश [Kh for rabbit], ग से गमला [G for flower pot], घ से घर [Gh for house]. Notice that each consonant carries a short a sound.

Step 4, Write with a headline. Every letter in क, ख, ग, घ hangs from a line drawn on top, called शिरोरेखा [the headline]. Write each letter three times: क क क, ख ख ख. Then read your line aloud: कमल, खरगोश, घर.

Step 5, Fix an error. A learner writes the letters of कमल without the top line, and confuses घ with ध. Correction: draw the line on top of every letter, and remember घ has a rounded head while ध has a straight bar on its left.
Step 6, Your turn: say and write च छ ज with one word each. Model answer: च से चम्मच [spoon], छ से छाता [umbrella], ज से जहाज़ [ship]. Write each letter three times with its headline.
Step 1, Meet the vowel signs on क. क (ka), का (kaa), कि (ki), की (kee), कु (ku), कू (koo), के (ke), कै (kai), को (ko), कौ (kau). The signs are matras: ा ि ी ु ू े ै ो ौ. Say each syllable aloud.

Step 2, Read words with long aa. काम [work], नाम [name], आम [mango], घास [grass]. The sign ा is a straight line after the letter. Compare कल [tomorrow] with काल [time]; the matra makes the sound longer.
Step 3, Short and long i, u. किताब [book] has the short ि, दीदी [elder sister] has the long ी, पुल [bridge] has the short ु, फूल [flower] has the long ू. The long sounds are held a little longer.
Step 4, Read words with e, ai, o, au. मेला [fair], तैरना [to swim], मोर [peacock], चौका [kitchen platform]. Sentence: मोर नाचता है। [The peacock dances.] Point at each matra as you read.

Step 5, Fix an error. A learner reads कि as ik, because the short i sign is written before the letter. Correction: ि is written before but read after the consonant, so कि is ki. Write किताब and read ki-taab.

Step 6, Your turn: read and write the words for mango, flower and book with their matras. Model answer: आम, फूल, किताब. Then add the correct matra: प_नी (water) should be पानी, using the long aa sign.

Step 1, Read two-letter words with no matras: जल [water], कल [tomorrow or yesterday], नल [tap], फल [fruit], घर [house], पल [a moment]. Sound out each consonant with its short a, then say the whole word smoothly.
Step 2, Add objects found in the classroom: कलम [pen], मेज़ [table], कुर्सी [chair], किताब [book], बस्ता [school bag]. Touch each object as you say its name, and read the label card aloud.
Step 3, Make sentences with है [is]. यह कलम है। [This is a pen.] वह घर है। [That is a house.] यह मेज़ है। [This is a table.] Replace the object with other words from your list.
Step 4, Short question and answer. यह क्या है? [What is this?] यह फल है। [This is a fruit.] वह क्या है? [What is that?] वह नल है। [That is a tap.] Ask your partner five times.
Step 5, Fix an error. A learner writes कमल when they mean pen. Correction: कलम is pen and कमल is lotus; the letters म and ल have swapped places. Read the word aloud to check meaning: क-ल-म is pen.
Step 6, Your turn: write one sentence about a chair and one about a school bag. Model answer: यह कुर्सी है। यह बस्ता है। [This is a chair. This is a school bag.] Check the headline over every letter.
Step 1, Listen to a short rhyme I made: नन्ही चींटी, चली कतार, दाना लेकर, घर के द्वार। [The little ant walked in a line, carrying a grain to the door of home.] Clap once on each stressed word.
Step 2, Find the rhyming words. कतार and द्वार end with the same sound आर. Other rhyming pairs: आम and शाम, बाग and आग, पल and जल. Say each pair twice and clap the rhythm.
Step 3, Learn the rhyme line by line. First say नन्ही चींटी, then चली कतार. Next say दाना लेकर, then घर के द्वार। Repeat the lines slowly, then at a steady walking speed, with hands marking the beat.
Step 4, Add actions. For नन्ही चींटी hold up a tiny finger. For चली कतार march on the spot. For दाना लेकर pretend to lift a grain. For घर के द्वार point to a door. Recite together as a group.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says दाना लेकर, कतार चली, changing the line order and losing the rhyme. Correction: keep the order नन्ही चींटी, चली कतार so that कतार and द्वार end the pair of lines.
Step 6, Your turn: make a two-line rhyme using आम and शाम. Model answer: मीठा आम, खाऊँ सुबह-शाम। [Sweet mango, I eat it morning and evening.] Recite it three times with a clap.

Step 1, Read three short words and write them from right to left. وَلَدٌ [a boy], بِنْتٌ [a girl], كِتَابٌ [a book]. Say the letters one by one, then blend them. Copy each word twice, joining the letters that join and lifting the pencil after ا and د.

Step 2, Build a sentence with هَذَا or هَذِهِ. هَذَا وَلَدٌ. [This is a boy.] هَذِهِ بِنْتٌ. [This is a girl.] هَذَا كِتَابٌ. [This is a book.] Use هَذَا for a masculine word and هَذِهِ for a feminine word.

Step 3, Add the word الْ [the] and a place. الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ. [The boy is in the house.] الْكِتَابُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ. [The book is on the table.] Read each sentence aloud and point to every word as you go.

Step 4, Say a sun-letter word. With الشَّمْسُ [the sun] the l of ال is not pronounced; we say ash-shams and the next letter has a shadda (ّ). Read: الشَّمْسُ سَاطِعَةٌ. [The sun is bright.] Compare الْقَمَرُ [the moon], where l is said.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes the words of a sentence joined together or reads الشَّمْسُ as al-shams. Correction: leave a space between words and read ash-shams. Also copy كِتَابٌ carefully: ك then ت then ا then ب, without losing the dots.

Step 6, Your turn: write a sentence saying the girl is in the house, and one for the sun. Model answer: الْبِنْتُ فِي الْبَيْتِ. [The girl is in the house.] الشَّمْسُ سَاطِعَةٌ. [The sun is bright.] Read both aloud.

Step 1, Name school objects. كِتَابٌ [book], قَلَمٌ [pen], دَفْتَرٌ [notebook], مِسْطَرَةٌ [ruler], حَقِيبَةٌ [bag], كُرْسِيٌّ [chair], طَاوِلَةٌ [table], سَبُّورَةٌ [board]. Touch each object and say: هَذَا قَلَمٌ، هَذِهِ مِسْطَرَةٌ. [This is a pen, this is a ruler.]

Step 2, Learn classroom commands to one boy. اجْلِسْ [Sit], قِفْ [Stand], افْتَحِ الْكِتَابَ [Open the book], أَغْلِقِ الْكِتَابَ [Close the book], اكْتُبْ [Write], اقْرَأْ [Read], اسْمَعْ [Listen]. Act each command as you say it.

Step 3, Change commands for a girl and for a group. For a girl: اجْلِسِي، قِفِي، اكْتُبِي [Sit, stand, write]. For the whole class: اجْلِسُوا، اكْتُبُوا [Sit, write]. The ending ـِي is for a girl and ـُوا for a group.

Step 4, Role-play a short dialogue. Student: أَيْنَ قَلَمِي؟ [Where is my pen?] Teacher: قَلَمُكَ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ. [Your pen is on the table.] Student: شُكْرًا. [Thank you.] Teacher: عَفْوًا. [You're welcome.] Swap roles and use a ruler or bag.
Step 5, Fix an error. A teacher tells a girl اجْلِسْ. Correction: to a girl say اجْلِسِي. Another error is saying هَذَا مِسْطَرَةٌ; مِسْطَرَةٌ is feminine, so say هَذِهِ مِسْطَرَةٌ [This is a ruler].

Step 6, Your turn: give three commands to a girl: stand, open the book, write. Model answer: قِفِي. افْتَحِي الْكِتَابَ. اكْتُبِي. [Stand. Open the book. Write.] Then ask where your bag is: أَيْنَ حَقِيبَتِي؟ [Where is my bag?]

Step 1, Learn fruit and food words. تُفَّاحٌ [apples], مَوْزٌ [bananas], بُرْتُقَالٌ [oranges], عِنَبٌ [grapes], خُبْزٌ [bread], حَلِيبٌ [milk], مَاءٌ [water], أَرُزٌ [rice]. Show picture cards and say each word with the right shape in your mouth.

Step 2, Say what you like. أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحَ. [I like apples.] أُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ. [I like bananas.] لَا أُحِبُّ الْحَلِيبَ. [I do not like milk.] The thing liked ends with a fatha sound: التُّفَّاحَ، الْمَوْزَ، الْحَلِيبَ.

Step 3, Ask a friend. هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْعِنَبَ؟ [Do you like grapes?] نَعَمْ، أُحِبُّهُ. [Yes, I like it.] لَا، لَا أُحِبُّهُ. [No, I do not like it.] Ask three classmates and record their answers on a tally sheet.

Step 4, Ask for food politely. Child: أُرِيدُ خُبْزًا مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. [I want some bread, please.] Seller: تَفَضَّلْ. [Here you are.] Child: شُكْرًا. [Thank you.] Seller: عَفْوًا. [You're welcome.] Replace خُبْزًا with مَاءً [water] or حَلِيبًا [milk].

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحُ with a damma ending. Correction: after أُحِبُّ the thing liked takes fatha, so say أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحَ. Remember to speak to a girl with مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.

Step 6, Your turn: say you like oranges and do not like rice, then ask for water. Model answer: أُحِبُّ الْبُرْتُقَالَ. لَا أُحِبُّ الْأَرُزَّ. أُرِيدُ مَاءً مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. [I like oranges. I do not like rice. I want water, please.]

Step 1, Listen to a tiny story I made. كَانَتْ قِطَّةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ تَلْعَبُ بِكُرَةٍ. [A small cat was playing with a ball.] تَدَحْرَجَتِ الْكُرَةُ تَحْتَ الْبَابِ. [The ball rolled under the door.] سَاعَدَتْهَا أُخْتُهَا. [Her sister helped her.] فَرِحَتِ الْقِطَّةُ. [The cat was happy.]

Step 2, Answer the question words about the story. مَنْ؟ [Who?] الْقِطَّةُ. [The cat.] مَاذَا؟ [What?] كُرَةٌ. [A ball.] أَيْنَ؟ [Where?] تَحْتَ الْبَابِ. [Under the door.] مَنْ سَاعَدَهَا؟ [Who helped her?] أُخْتُهَا. [Her sister.]

Step 3, Retell with sequence words. أَوَّلًا، لَعِبَتِ الْقِطَّةُ. [First, the cat played.] ثُمَّ تَدَحْرَجَتِ الْكُرَةُ. [Then the ball rolled.] فِي النِّهَايَةِ، فَرِحَتِ الْقِطَّةُ. [In the end, the cat was happy.] Say the three sentences without looking.

Step 4, Sing a simple counting chant. وَاحِدٌ، اثْنَانِ، قِطَّةٌ تَلْعَبُ الْآنَ. [One, two, a cat is playing now.] Clap on each word and repeat. Add actions: roll your hands like a ball for تَلْعَبُ.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says كَانَ قِطَّةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ with the masculine verb. Correction: the cat is feminine, so the verb takes the feminine ending: كَانَتْ قِطَّةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ. Say each feminine past verb with the ending ـَتْ.

Step 6, Your turn: retell the story in your own words using أَوَّلًا and فِي النِّهَايَةِ. Model answer: أَوَّلًا، لَعِبَتِ الْقِطَّةُ بِالْكُرَةِ. فِي النِّهَايَةِ، سَاعَدَتْهَا أُخْتُهَا. [First, the cat played with the ball. In the end, her sister helped her.]

Step 1, Learn family words with my. mon père [my father], ma mère [my mother], mon frère [my brother], ma sœur [my sister], mon grand-père, ma grand-mère [my grandfather, my grandmother]. Use mon with masculine nouns and ma with feminine nouns.

Step 2, Introduce your family. Voici ma famille. [Here is my family.] Voici mon frère. Il s'appelle Paul. [Here is my brother. His name is Paul.] Voici ma sœur. Elle s'appelle Nina. [Here is my sister. Her name is Nina.] Use il for a boy and elle for a girl.

Step 3, Talk about friends. Voici mon ami Hugo et mon amie Sara. [Here are my friend Hugo and my friend Sara.] Nous jouons ensemble. [We play together.] Note mon amie: before a vowel sound even a feminine noun takes mon.

Step 4, Short dialogue. Léa : C'est qui ? [Who is it?] Tom : C'est ma grand-mère. Elle s'appelle Rose. [It is my grandmother. Her name is Rose.] Léa : Elle est gentille ! [She is kind!] Tom : Oui, je l'aime beaucoup. [Yes, I love her very much.]
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says ma frère. Correction: mon frère, because frère is masculine. Another slip is mon mère; say ma mère. Check the noun first, then choose mon or ma.

Step 6, Your turn: introduce your mother and your brother with their names. Model answer: Voici ma mère. Elle s'appelle Amina. Voici mon frère. Il s'appelle Yanis. [Here is my mother. Her name is Amina. Here is my brother. His name is Yanis.]

Step 1, Name school objects with un or une. un cahier [a notebook], un stylo [a pen], un livre [a book], une règle [a ruler], une trousse [a pencil case], une chaise [a chair], une table [a table]. Point to each and say its name.

Step 2, Ask and answer. Qu'est-ce que c'est ? [What is it?] C'est une règle. [It is a ruler.] C'est un cahier. [It is a notebook.] Ask about five objects in your classroom and answer with C'est un or C'est une.

Step 3, Say where things are. Où est ma trousse ? [Where is my pencil case?] Elle est dans mon sac. [It is in my bag.] Où est mon livre ? [Where is my book?] Il est sur la table. [It is on the table.] Use dans [in], sur [on], sous [under].

Step 4, Learn classroom instructions. Ouvrez vos livres. [Open your books.] Fermez vos cahiers. [Close your notebooks.] Asseyez-vous. [Sit down.] Écoutez, s'il vous plaît. [Listen, please.] Respond with the action and say Oui, madame.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says C'est un règle. Correction: C'est une règle, because règle is feminine. Another slip is Il est dans mon sac for a trousse; use Elle est dans mon sac, because trousse is feminine.

Step 6, Your turn: say what a ruler is and where your pen is. Model answer: C'est une règle. Mon stylo est sur la table. [It is a ruler. My pen is on the table.] Then give a command: Ouvrez vos cahiers. [Open your notebooks.]
Step 1, Name animals. le chat [the cat], le chien [the dog], le cheval [the horse], la vache [the cow], l'oiseau [the bird], le poisson [the fish]. Say each one and make its sound or movement.
Step 2, Name body parts. la tête [head], le nez [nose], la bouche [mouth], la main [hand], le pied [foot], les yeux [eyes], les bras [arms], les jambes [legs]. Touch each part as you say it.

Step 3, Describe with avoir. J'ai deux yeux et un nez. [I have two eyes and a nose.] Le chien a quatre pattes. [The dog has four legs.] L'oiseau a deux ailes. [The bird has two wings.] Use a for he or she has.
Step 4, Ask and answer. Tu as un animal ? [Do you have a pet?] Oui, j'ai un chat. Il s'appelle Noisette. [Yes, I have a cat. His name is Noisette.] Il est petit et noir. [He is small and black.]
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says deux œil. Correction: deux yeux, because œil [eye] has an irregular plural. Another slip is saying the final s in les bras; in les bras the s of bras is silent.

Step 6, Your turn: say your pet has four legs and a long tail, and that you have two hands. Model answer: Mon chien a quatre pattes et une longue queue. J'ai deux mains. [My dog has four legs and a long tail. I have two hands.]

Step 1, Learn a short rhyme I made. Un, deux, trois, quatre, je tape des mains. [One, two, three, four, I clap my hands.] Cinq, six, sept, huit, je dis bonjour au matin. [Five, six, seven, eight, I say hello to the morning.] Clap on each number.

Step 2, Work out the meaning line by line. je tape des mains means I clap my hands. je dis bonjour means I say hello. au matin means in the morning. Mime each action slowly, then say the line again with a steady beat.

Step 3, Notice the rhyme. mains and matin end with a similar sound, the nasal in. Other pairs with the same sound: main and pain, chien and bien. Say each pair twice, making the sound come through the nose.

Step 4, Perform in two groups. Group A sings Un, deux, trois, quatre, je tape des mains. Group B answers Cinq, six, sept, huit, je dis bonjour au matin. Then everyone sings both lines together, faster each time.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says the s in mains and the t is dropped in huit. Correction: in mains the s is silent, but in huit you hear the t, so say weet. Count again from un to dix with correct sounds.

Step 6, Your turn: make a second verse with the days using the same tune. Model answer: Lundi, mardi, je saute bien. Mercredi, jeudi, je chante bien. [Monday, Tuesday, I jump well. Wednesday, Thursday, I sing well.]

Step 1, Learn family words: माँ [mother], पिताजी [father], भाई [brother], बहन [sister], दादा [paternal grandfather], दादी [paternal grandmother], नाना [maternal grandfather], नानी [maternal grandmother], चाचा [paternal uncle]. Say each word and point to a family photo.

Step 2, Use मेरा, मेरी, मेरे [my]. मेरा भाई [my brother], मेरी बहन [my sister], मेरी माँ [my mother], मेरे पिताजी [my father]. Match with the noun: मेरा for a masculine noun, मेरी for a feminine noun, मेरे for a respectful or plural one.

Step 3, Introduce people. यह मेरी माँ हैं। [This is my mother.] ये मेरे दादाजी हैं। [This is my grandfather.] यह मेरा भाई है। [This is my brother.] वह मेरी बहन है। [That is my sister.] Elders take हैं as a mark of respect.

Step 4, Ask and answer. तुम्हारे घर में कौन-कौन है? [Who is in your house?] मेरे घर में माँ, पिताजी, दादी और मैं हैं। [In my house there are mother, father, grandmother and I.] घर में चार लोग हैं। [There are four people in the house.]
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says मेरा बहन. Correction: मेरी बहन, because बहन is feminine. Another slip is मेरी भाई; say मेरा भाई. Look at the noun first, then pick मेरा or मेरी.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences introducing your mother, brother and grandmother. Model answer: यह मेरी माँ हैं। यह मेरा भाई है। ये मेरी दादी हैं। [This is my mother. This is my brother. This is my grandmother.]

Step 1, Learn colours: लाल [red], नीला [blue], हरा [green], पीला [yellow], सफ़ेद [white], काला [black], गुलाबी [pink], नारंगी [orange]. Hold up crayons and ask: यह कौन-सा रंग है? [Which colour is this?] Answer: यह लाल है। [This is red.]
Step 2, Count from 1 to 10: एक, दो, तीन, चार, पाँच, छह, सात, आठ, नौ, दस. Then 11 to 20: ग्यारह, बारह, तेरह, चौदह, पंद्रह, सोलह, सत्रह, अठारह, उन्नीस, बीस. Count marbles, and say each number aloud.

Step 3, Make sentences. मेरे पास पाँच लाल गुब्बारे हैं। [I have five red balloons.] टोकरी में बारह आम हैं। [There are twelve mangoes in the basket.] आसमान नीला है। [The sky is blue.] Count and describe objects around you.

Step 4, Match colour words to the noun. हरा तोता [a green parrot], हरी मिर्च [a green chilli], हरे पत्ते [green leaves]. Colours ending in आ change: हरा for a masculine noun, हरी for a feminine noun, हरे for a plural masculine noun.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says हरा मिर्च. Correction: हरी मिर्च, because मिर्च is feminine. Also सत्रह is the number for 17 and अठारह is 18; keep the two apart by listening to the middle sound.

Step 6, Your turn: say you have fifteen yellow flowers and a blue bag. Model answer: मेरे पास पंद्रह पीले फूल हैं। मेरा बस्ता नीला है। [I have fifteen yellow flowers. My bag is blue.] Notice पीले agrees with the plural फूल.

Step 1, Name animals: शेर [lion], हाथी [elephant], बंदर [monkey], गाय [cow], कुत्ता [dog], बिल्ली [cat]. Then birds: तोता [parrot], मोर [peacock], कौआ [crow], चिड़िया [sparrow], कबूतर [pigeon]. Say each word and imitate the creature.

Step 2, Describe them in short sentences. हाथी बड़ा है। [The elephant is big.] तोता हरा है। [The parrot is green.] बिल्ली छोटी है। [The cat is small.] शेर दहाड़ता है। [The lion roars.] Notice बड़ा, छोटी change with the noun.

Step 3, Say what animals do. गाय दूध देती है। [The cow gives milk.] कौआ काँव-काँव करता है। [The crow caws.] मोर नाचता है। [The peacock dances.] चिड़िया पेड़ पर बैठी है। [The sparrow is sitting on the tree.]
Step 4, Ask and answer. तुम्हें कौन-सा जानवर पसंद है? [Which animal do you like?] मुझे हाथी पसंद है। [I like the elephant.] क्यों? [Why?] क्योंकि वह बहुत बड़ा है। [Because he is very big.]
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says तोता बैठी है. Correction: तोता बैठा है, because तोता is masculine. Likewise say चिड़िया बैठी है, because चिड़िया is feminine, not चिड़िया बैठा है.
Step 6, Your turn: write about a peacock and a cat. Model answer: मोर सुंदर है। वह नाचता है। बिल्ली छोटी है। वह दूध पीती है। [The peacock is beautiful. It dances. The cat is small. It drinks milk.]

Step 1, Learn the order of a Hindi sentence: who, what, action. मीना किताब पढ़ती है। [Meena reads a book.] Here मीना is the doer, किताब is the thing, पढ़ती है is the action. The action comes at the end.

Step 2, Make more sentences. रवि गेंद खेलता है। [Ravi plays with a ball.] माँ रोटी बनाती है। [Mother makes roti.] मैं पानी पीता हूँ। [I drink water, said by a boy.] मैं पानी पीती हूँ। [I drink water, said by a girl.]

Step 3, End sentences correctly. A full stop in Hindi is a vertical line। not a dot. Write: बच्चे स्कूल जाते हैं। [Children go to school.] Check that every sentence starts with a capital-like clear word and ends with the vertical line.

Step 4, Describe a picture. चित्र में एक लड़की है। [In the picture there is a girl.] वह फूल तोड़ती है। [She picks a flower.] पास में एक कुत्ता है। [Nearby there is a dog.] वह भौंकता है। [He barks.] Look at each picture and say three sentences.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes पढ़ती मीना किताब है. Correction: मीना किताब पढ़ती है। The action word should be at the end. Also check that the verb matches the doer: लड़का खेलता है, लड़की खेलती है.
Step 6, Your turn: write two sentences about a boy who drinks milk and a girl who reads. Model answer: लड़का दूध पीता है। लड़की किताब पढ़ती है। [The boy drinks milk. The girl reads a book.]

Step 1, Read this short passage I wrote. أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْمَدْرَسَةَ. فِي صَفِّي عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا. مُعَلِّمَتِي تَقْرَأُ لَنَا قِصَّةً كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. [I love school. In my class there are twenty students. My teacher reads us a story every day.] Read it twice, then underline the numbers.

Step 2, Find the key words. الْمَدْرَسَةُ [school], صَفٌّ [class], طَالِبٌ [student], قِصَّةٌ [story], كُلَّ يَوْمٍ [every day]. Say what each sentence is about before answering. The first is about liking school, the second about the class, the third about the story.

Step 3, Answer questions with a full sentence. كَمْ طَالِبًا فِي الصَّفِّ؟ [How many students are in the class?] فِي الصَّفِّ عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا. [In the class there are twenty students.] مَاذَا تَقْرَأُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ؟ [What does the teacher read?] تَقْرَأُ قِصَّةً. [She reads a story.]

Step 4, Ask a when-question. مَتَى تَقْرَأُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ الْقِصَّةَ؟ [When does the teacher read the story?] تَقْرَأُهَا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. [She reads it every day.] Notice how the answer repeats words from the text, which proves you found it in the passage.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student answers the question كَمْ طَالِبًا فِي الصَّفِّ؟ with the single word كَثِيرٌ [many]. Correction: go back to the text; the number is عِشْرُونَ, so the full answer is عِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا. Guessing is not reading.

Step 6, Your turn: answer who reads us a story and where is the class. Model answer: مُعَلِّمَتِي تَقْرَأُ لَنَا قِصَّةً. [My teacher reads us a story.] ثُمَّ: أَنَا فِي الصَّفِّ فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [I am in the class at school.] Check you copied the spelling.

Step 1, Know what a noun is. الِاسْمُ [the noun] names a person, thing or place: وَلَدٌ [boy], كِتَابٌ [book], مَدْرَسَةٌ [school]. A quick test: you can put الْ before a noun, as in الْكِتَابُ [the book]. Collect five nouns from your bag.

Step 2, Know what a verb is. الْفِعْلُ [the verb] shows an action. Past: كَتَبَ [he wrote], ذَهَبَ [he went], جَلَسَ [he sat]. Present: يَكْتُبُ [he writes], يَذْهَبُ [he goes], يَجْلِسُ [he sits]. You cannot say الْ before a verb.

Step 3, Put them together. الْوَلَدُ يَقْرَأُ الْكِتَابَ. [The boy reads the book.] ذَهَبَتِ الْبِنْتُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [The girl went to school.] In the first sentence الْوَلَدُ and الْكِتَابَ are nouns and يَقْرَأُ is the verb.

Step 4, Sort a list. قَلَمٌ، يَرْسُمُ، بِنْتٌ، أَكَلَ، شَجَرَةٌ. [pen, he draws, girl, he ate, tree] Nouns: قَلَمٌ، بِنْتٌ، شَجَرَةٌ. Verbs: يَرْسُمُ، أَكَلَ. Each noun can take الْ; the verbs cannot.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child labels يَلْعَبُ [he plays] as a noun. Correction: it is a verb, because it shows an action and الْيَلْعَبُ is impossible. Another error is calling كُرَةٌ [ball] a verb; كُرَةٌ names a thing, so it is a noun.

Step 6, Your turn: write a sentence with the noun بِنْتٌ and the verb تَرْسُمُ [she draws], then name noun and verb. Model answer: الْبِنْتُ تَرْسُمُ شَجَرَةً. [The girl draws a tree.] Nouns: الْبِنْتُ، شَجَرَةً. Verb: تَرْسُمُ.

Step 1, Describe your morning in the present. أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ. [I wake up at seven o'clock.] أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي. [I wash my face.] أَتَنَاوَلُ الْفُطُورَ. [I have breakfast.] أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [I go to school.] Say them in order.

Step 2, Describe the rest of the day. أَعُودُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ. [I return home.] أَكْتُبُ وَاجِبِي. [I do my homework.] أَلْعَبُ مَعَ أَخِي. [I play with my brother.] أَنَامُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ. [I sleep at nine o'clock.]

Step 3, Describe a trip to the beach in the past. ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. [We went to the beach.] لَعِبْتُ بِالرَّمْلِ. [I played with the sand.] سَبَحَ أَخِي فِي الْبَحْرِ. [My brother swam in the sea.] كَانَ الْجَوُّ جَمِيلًا. [The weather was beautiful.]

Step 4, Compare present and past. الْيَوْمَ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [Today I go to school.] أَمْسِ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. [Yesterday I went to the beach.] The present verb begins with أَ for I; the past verb ends with تُ for I.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says أَمْسِ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. Correction: أَمْسِ [yesterday] needs the past, so say أَمْسِ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ. Match the time word with the right verb form every time.

Step 6, Your turn: write about your morning and yesterday's trip, two sentences each. Model answer: أَسْتَيْقِظُ مُبَكِّرًا وَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. أَمْسِ ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الشَّاطِئِ وَلَعِبْتُ بِالرَّمْلِ. [I wake up early and go to school. Yesterday we went to the beach and I played in the sand.]

Step 1, A good short text has three connected sentences: what, then what, and why or how I felt. Plan before you write. Topic: a visit to the park. Sentence one says where, sentence two says what you did, sentence three says how you felt.
Step 2, Write sentence one. ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْحَدِيقَةِ مَعَ أُسْرَتِي. [I went to the park with my family.] Begin with a clear verb and add a place. Put a full stop at the end of the sentence.

Step 3, Write sentence two with a linking word. ثُمَّ لَعِبْتُ مَعَ صَدِيقِي بِالْكُرَةِ. [Then I played with my friend with the ball.] ثُمَّ means then. Other linking words are وَ [and] and بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ [after that].

Step 4, Write sentence three with a reason. كُنْتُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنَّ الْجَوَّ كَانَ جَمِيلًا. [I was happy because the weather was beautiful.] لِأَنَّ means because. Now read all three together: ذَهَبْتُ... ثُمَّ... كُنْتُ سَعِيدًا...

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes ذَهَبْتُ الْحَدِيقَةِ لَعِبْتُ سَعِيدًا. Correction: add إِلَى [to], a linking word and a reason, so the text reads clearly: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْحَدِيقَةِ. ثُمَّ لَعِبْتُ. كُنْتُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنَّ الْجَوَّ جَمِيلٌ.

Step 6, Your turn: write three connected sentences about a trip to the market. Model answer: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى السُّوقِ مَعَ أُمِّي. ثُمَّ اشْتَرَيْنَا الْفَاكِهَةَ. كُنْتُ سَعِيدًا لِأَنِّي أُحِبُّ التُّفَّاحَ. [I went to the market with my mother. Then we bought fruit. I was happy because I love apples.]

Step 1, Present your friend with name and age. Voici mon ami Karim. [Here is my friend Karim.] Il a huit ans. [He is eight years old.] Voici mon amie Inès. [Here is my friend Inès.] Elle a neuf ans. [She is nine years old.] Use il for a boy and elle for a girl.

Step 2, Describe what he or she looks like. Karim est grand et il a les cheveux noirs. [Karim is tall and has black hair.] Inès est petite et elle a les yeux bleus. [Inès is small and has blue eyes.] Notice petite takes an e because Inès is a girl.

Step 3, Describe character and likes. Karim est gentil et drôle. [Karim is kind and funny.] Il aime le football. [He likes football.] Inès est sportive. [Inès is sporty.] Elle aime la danse. [She likes dancing.] Add one thing you do together.

Step 4, A short dialogue. Maman : Comment est ton ami ? [What is your friend like?] Léo : Il est grand et très sympa. [He is tall and very nice.] Maman : Comment il s'appelle ? [What is his name?] Léo : Il s'appelle Karim. [His name is Karim.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says Inès est grand. Correction: Inès est grande, because Inès is a girl and the adjective adds an e. Another slip is Il a neuf ans for a person who is nine and called Inès; say Elle a neuf ans.

Step 6, Your turn: present a friend named Samir, ten years old, short, kind, who likes drawing. Model answer: Voici mon ami Samir. Il a dix ans. Il est petit et gentil. Il aime dessiner. [Here is my friend Samir. He is ten. He is small and kind. He likes drawing.]

Step 1, Learn avoir [to have]: j'ai, tu as, il a, elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont, elles ont. Example: J'ai un frère. [I have a brother.] Nous avons un chat. [We have a cat.] Say the full row aloud with a pointing finger.

Step 2, Learn être [to be]: je suis, tu es, il est, elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont, elles sont. Example: Je suis content. [I am happy.] Elles sont à l'école. [They are at school.] Say the full row aloud.

Step 3, Choose between them. Use être for what someone is: Il est grand. [He is tall.] Use avoir for age and possessions: J'ai dix ans. [I am ten.] Elle a une bicyclette. [She has a bicycle.] Make three sentences with each verb.

Step 4, Dialogue. Amir : Tu as quel âge ? [How old are you?] Nadia : J'ai neuf ans. Et toi ? [I am nine. And you?] Amir : J'ai dix ans. Nous sommes amis ! [I am ten. We are friends!] Nadia : Oui, nous sommes dans la même classe. [Yes, we are in the same class.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says Je suis dix ans. Correction: J'ai dix ans. Another says Il a content. Correction: Il est content. Also keep ont and sont apart: Ils ont un chat [They have a cat] but Ils sont contents [They are happy].

Step 6, Your turn: write about yourself using three forms of avoir and three of être. Model answer: Je suis Maya. J'ai huit ans. Mon frère a six ans. Nous sommes contents. Ils sont gentils. [I am Maya. I am eight. My brother is six. We are happy. They are kind.]

Step 1, Feminine adds an e. grand [tall, masculine] becomes grande [feminine]; petit becomes petite; content becomes contente; vert becomes verte. Say each pair aloud and listen for the final consonant. In petit the t is silent, in petite it is heard.

Step 2, Plural adds an s. un chat noir [a black cat] becomes des chats noirs [black cats]. une maison blanche [a white house] becomes des maisons blanches [white houses]. The adjective agrees in gender and number with the noun.

Step 3, Put it in position. Many short, common adjectives go before the noun: un petit chat, une grande maison, un bon livre. Colour adjectives go after: un chat noir, une voiture rouge. Say these four phrases aloud with their pictures.

Step 4, Describe a picture. Voici une petite maison blanche. [Here is a small white house.] Il y a deux grands arbres verts. [There are two tall green trees.] Dans le jardin, il y a des chats noirs. [In the garden there are black cats.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says des chats noir. Correction: des chats noirs, because chats is plural. Another says une maison petit. Correction: une petite maison; the adjective must be feminine and goes before maison.

Step 6, Your turn: describe two girls who are tall and kind, and a small black dog. Model answer: Les filles sont grandes et gentilles. J'ai un petit chien noir. [The girls are tall and kind. I have a small black dog.] Check each adjective ending.

Step 1, Say what you like to do. J'aime jouer au football. [I like to play football.] J'aime lire. [I like to read.] J'aime dessiner. [I like to draw.] After j'aime we use the infinitive, the form ending in er, ir or re.

Step 2, Use jouer à and faire de. Je joue au tennis. [I play tennis.] Je joue à la balle. [I play with a ball.] Je fais du vélo. [I ride a bike.] Je fais de la natation. [I swim.] à plus le becomes au; de plus le becomes du.

Step 3, Say how often and when. Le samedi, je joue avec mes amis. [On Saturdays I play with my friends.] Le soir, je lis un livre. [In the evening I read a book.] Je regarde la télé le dimanche. [I watch TV on Sundays.]

Step 4, Dialogue. Sami : Qu'est-ce que tu fais le week-end ? [What do you do at the weekend?] Lina : Je fais du vélo avec mon père. [I ride my bike with my father.] Sami : Moi, je joue au foot. [I play football.] Lina : On peut jouer ensemble ! [We can play together!]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says Je joue le football. Correction: Je joue au football. Another says Je fais le vélo. Correction: Je fais du vélo. Remember that these verbs need à or de before the activity.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences about your hobbies using jouer, faire and aimer. Model answer: Je joue au basket. Je fais de la danse. J'aime lire des histoires. [I play basketball. I do dance. I like reading stories.]

Step 1, Read this short passage I wrote. सुबह का समय था। गीता अपनी दादी के साथ बगीचे में गई। वहाँ गुलाब के फूल खिले थे। गीता ने दादी के लिए एक फूल तोड़ा। [It was morning. Geeta went to the garden with her grandmother. Rose flowers were blooming there. Geeta picked a flower for her grandmother.]

Step 2, Understand the sentences. सुबह का समय था [It was morning] tells when. बगीचे में [in the garden] tells where. गुलाब के फूल [rose flowers] tells what. दादी के लिए [for grandmother] tells for whom. Find these words in the text.

Step 3, Answer questions in full sentences. गीता किसके साथ गई? [Who did Geeta go with?] गीता अपनी दादी के साथ गई। [Geeta went with her grandmother.] फूल कहाँ खिले थे? [Where were the flowers blooming?] फूल बगीचे में खिले थे। [The flowers were blooming in the garden.]

Step 4, Find the reason or result. गीता ने फूल किसके लिए तोड़ा? [For whom did Geeta pick the flower?] उसने दादी के लिए फूल तोड़ा। [She picked the flower for her grandmother.] Always take the answer from the passage, using its own words.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child answers फूल कहाँ खिले थे? with तालाब में [in the pond]. Correction: reread; the text says बगीचे में, so the answer is फूल बगीचे में खिले थे। Another error is leaving out the final vertical line; end every answer with।

Step 6, Your turn: answer what time it was and what Geeta did. Model answer: सुबह का समय था। गीता ने दादी के लिए एक फूल तोड़ा। [It was morning. Geeta picked a flower for her grandmother.] Both answers come directly from the passage.

Step 1, A noun (संज्ञा) names a person, animal, thing or place. Each Hindi noun is masculine (पुल्लिंग) or feminine (स्त्रीलिंग). लड़का [boy] and घोड़ा [horse] are masculine. लड़की [girl] and चिड़िया [bird] are feminine.

Step 2, Use the ending as a clue. Many masculine nouns end in ा: लड़का, कमरा [room], बस्ता [bag]. Many feminine nouns end in ी: रोटी, कुर्सी, घड़ी [watch]. Make pairs: बेटा and बेटी, घोड़ा and घोड़ी. Say them aloud.

Step 3, Learn the exceptions. पानी [water], हाथी [elephant] and दही [curd] end in ी but are masculine: हाथी बड़ा है। [The elephant is big.] मेज़ [table] and किताब [book] are feminine: किताब अच्छी है। [The book is good.]

Step 4, Show gender through the verb. लड़का खेलता है। [The boy plays.] लड़की खेलती है। [The girl plays.] The verb ending changes from ता to ती. Sort these: फूल, मेज़, पेड़, कुर्सी. Masculine: फूल, पेड़. Feminine: मेज़, कुर्सी.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says यह मेज़ अच्छा है। Correction: यह मेज़ अच्छी है। because मेज़ is feminine. Another says पानी ठंडी है। Correction: पानी ठंडा है। because पानी is masculine.

Step 6, Your turn: name the gender of घड़ी, बस्ता, चिड़िया and घोड़ा. Model answer: घड़ी is feminine, बस्ता is masculine, चिड़िया is feminine, घोड़ा is masculine. Then write: घड़ी सुंदर है। [The watch is beautiful.] with the matching ending.

Step 1, Read a four-line poem I made. काले बादल, गरजे ज़ोर, नाचे जंगल में हर मोर। छम-छम बूँदें, मीठी तान, खुश हुआ सारा जहान। [Black clouds thunder loudly, every peacock dances in the forest. Pitter-patter drops, a sweet tune, the whole world is happy.]

Step 2, Understand the rhyme. ज़ोर and मोर rhyme, and तान and जहान end with the same sound ान. Mark the rhyming ends with a pencil. Say the lines with a steady beat, and slow down at the rhyming words.

Step 3, Recite with expression. Say गरजे ज़ोर loudly and छम-छम बूँदें softly. Use your hands to show the clouds. Speak clearly, say each word in full, and pause at each comma. Recite twice, then try without the book.

Step 4, Now retell a tiny story. एक नन्हा बीज था। उसे मिट्टी में बो दिया गया। बारिश हुई और वह पौधा बन गया। [There was a tiny seed. It was sown in the soil. It rained and it became a plant.] Use pehle, phir, ant mein: पहले, फिर, अंत में.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child retells the story as बारिश हुई, बीज बन गया पौधा, मिट्टी में बोया. Correction: tell it in order: पहले बीज को मिट्टी में बोया गया, फिर बारिश हुई, अंत में वह पौधा बन गया।

Step 6, Your turn: say the story again using पहले, फिर and अंत में. Model answer: पहले एक नन्हा बीज मिट्टी में बोया गया। फिर बारिश हुई। अंत में बीज पौधा बन गया। [First a tiny seed was sown. Then it rained. Finally the seed became a plant.]

Step 1, Look at a picture of a park with children, a swing, a dog and a girl with a ball. Name what you see: बच्चे [children], झूला [swing], कुत्ता [dog], गेंद [ball], लड़की [girl]. Make a word list before writing sentences.

Step 2, Write what is there. चित्र में एक पार्क है। [In the picture there is a park.] वहाँ एक झूला है। [There is a swing there.] पास में एक कुत्ता बैठा है। [Nearby a dog is sitting.] Use है for one thing and हैं for many.

Step 3, Write what is happening with रहा, रही, रहे. बच्चे झूला झूल रहे हैं। [The children are swinging.] लड़की गेंद से खेल रही है। [The girl is playing with a ball.] कुत्ता भाग रहा है। [The dog is running.]

Step 4, Add colour and feeling. लड़की की गेंद लाल है। [The girl's ball is red.] सब बहुत खुश हैं। [Everyone is very happy.] Put the sentences in order: place first, then what people do, then how they feel.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes लड़की खेल रहा है। Correction: लड़की खेल रही है। because लड़की is feminine. Another writes बच्चे झूल रहा हैं। Correction: बच्चे झूल रहे हैं। because बच्चे is plural.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences about a picture of a market with a woman buying mangoes. Model answer: चित्र में एक बाज़ार है। एक औरत आम खरीद रही है। दुकानदार आम तौल रहा है। [In the picture there is a market. A woman is buying mangoes. The shopkeeper is weighing mangoes.]

Step 1, Name the four seasons. الرَّبِيعُ [spring], الصَّيْفُ [summer], الْخَرِيفُ [autumn], الشِّتَاءُ [winter]. Say them in order and point to a calendar. Notice that الرَّبِيعُ, الصَّيْفُ and الشِّتَاءُ start with a sun letter, so the l of الْ is silent.

Step 2, Learn weather words. الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ [The weather is hot]. الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ [cold]. الْجَوُّ مُعْتَدِلٌ [mild]. الْجَوُّ مُمْطِرٌ [rainy]. الْجَوُّ مُشْمِسٌ [sunny]. Ask: كَيْفَ الْجَوُّ الْيَوْمَ؟ [How is the weather today?]

Step 3, Describe each season. فِي الصَّيْفِ يَكُونُ الْجَوُّ حَارًّا. [In summer the weather is hot.] فِي الشِّتَاءِ تَهْطِلُ الْأَمْطَارُ. [In winter rain falls.] فِي الرَّبِيعِ تُزْهِرُ الْأَزْهَارُ. [In spring flowers bloom.] فِي الْخَرِيفِ تَسْقُطُ أَوْرَاقُ الْأَشْجَارِ. [In autumn the leaves fall.]

Step 4, Short dialogue. سَلْمَى: كَيْفَ الْجَوُّ الْيَوْمَ؟ [How is the weather today?] عُمَرُ: الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ وَمُمْطِرٌ. [The weather is cold and rainy.] سَلْمَى: أَيُّ فَصْلٍ تُحِبُّ؟ [Which season do you like?] عُمَرُ: أُحِبُّ الرَّبِيعَ. [I like spring.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says الْجَوُّ حَارَّةٌ. Correction: الْجَوُّ is masculine, so say الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ. But for a feminine noun use the feminine form: الشَّمْسُ حَارَّةٌ [The sun is hot]. Match the adjective to its noun.

Step 6, Your turn: write two sentences about your favourite season and its weather. Model answer: أُحِبُّ الشِّتَاءَ لِأَنَّ الْأَمْطَارَ تَهْطِلُ. الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ وَأَلْبَسُ مِعْطَفًا. [I like winter because rain falls. The weather is cold and I wear a coat.]

Step 1, Name things in a garden. حَدِيقَةٌ [garden], شَجَرَةٌ [tree], وَرْدَةٌ [rose], عُشْبٌ [grass], فَرَاشَةٌ [butterfly], نَحْلَةٌ [bee], عُصْفُورٌ [sparrow], أَرْنَبٌ [rabbit]. Label a picture with these words.

Step 2, Describe with adjectives that agree. شَجَرَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ [a big tree], وَرْدَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ [a beautiful rose], أَرْنَبٌ صَغِيرٌ [a small rabbit]. The adjective copies the gender of the noun and adds ـَةٌ for a feminine noun.

Step 3, Say what is in the garden. فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ شَجَرَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ. [In the garden there is a big tree.] تَقِفُ عَلَيْهَا عَصَافِيرُ. [Sparrows stand on it.] الْفَرَاشَةُ تَطِيرُ بَيْنَ الْأَزْهَارِ. [The butterfly flies among the flowers.]

Step 4, Say what animals do. الْأَرْنَبُ يَأْكُلُ الْجَزَرَ. [The rabbit eats carrots.] النَّحْلَةُ تَجْمَعُ الرَّحِيقَ. [The bee collects nectar.] Ask: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ النَّحْلَةُ؟ [What does the bee do?] تَجْمَعُ الرَّحِيقَ. [It collects nectar.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says وَرْدَةٌ جَمِيلٌ. Correction: وَرْدَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ, because وَرْدَةٌ is feminine. Another says أَرْنَبٌ صَغِيرَةٌ. Correction: أَرْنَبٌ صَغِيرٌ, because أَرْنَبٌ is masculine.

Step 6, Your turn: describe a garden with a white rabbit and a red rose. Model answer: فِي حَدِيقَتِي أَرْنَبٌ أَبْيَضُ وَوَرْدَةٌ حَمْرَاءُ. الْأَرْنَبُ يَأْكُلُ الْعُشْبَ. [In my garden there is a white rabbit and a red rose. The rabbit eats grass.]

Step 1, Learn question words. مَا [what], مَنْ [who], أَيْنَ [where], مَتَى [when], كَمْ [how many], لِمَاذَا [why], كَيْفَ [how]. Say each with a pointing hand. Remember مَنْ asks about people and مَا about things.

Step 2, Ask personal questions to a boy. مَا اسْمُكَ؟ [What is your name?] كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ [How old are you?] أَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟ [Where do you live?] مَاذَا تُحِبُّ؟ [What do you like?] To a girl the endings change: مَا اسْمُكِ؟ كَمْ عُمْرُكِ؟

Step 3, Answer in a full sentence. اسْمِي سَلْمَى. [My name is Salma.] عُمْرِي تِسْعُ سَنَوَاتٍ. [I am nine years old.] أَسْكُنُ فِي مَدِينَةٍ كَبِيرَةٍ. [I live in a big city.] أُحِبُّ الْقِرَاءَةَ. [I like reading.]

Step 4, Practise a conversation. عَلِيٌّ: مَرْحَبًا، مَا اسْمُكِ؟ [Hello, what is your name?] سَلْمَى: اسْمِي سَلْمَى، وَمَا اسْمُكَ؟ [My name is Salma, and yours?] عَلِيٌّ: اسْمِي عَلِيٌّ. أَيْنَ تَسْكُنِينَ؟ [My name is Ali. Where do you live?] سَلْمَى: أَسْكُنُ فِي الْحَيِّ الْقَدِيمِ. [I live in the old quarter.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child asks مَنْ اسْمُكَ؟ Correction: مَا اسْمُكَ؟ because a name is a thing, not a person. Another answers the question كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ with أَنَا مِنْ مِصْرَ; reply with the age, عُمْرِي عَشْرُ سَنَوَاتٍ [I am ten years old].

Step 6, Your turn: ask a new classmate two questions and answer two yourself. Model answer: مَا اسْمُكَ؟ وَأَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟ اسْمِي مَرْيَمُ، وَأَسْكُنُ بِجَانِبِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [What is your name? And where do you live? My name is Maryam, and I live next to the school.]

Step 1, A verb tells an action. Learn five: खाना [to eat], पीना [to drink], पढ़ना [to read], खेलना [to play], जाना [to go]. Remove ना to get the stem: खा, पी, पढ़, खेल, जा. Say each stem and each full verb.

Step 2, Make the present tense: stem + ता, ती or ते, plus है, हूँ or हैं. मैं स्कूल जाता हूँ। [I go to school, a boy speaking.] मैं स्कूल जाती हूँ। [A girl speaking.] वह खेलता है। [He plays.] हम पढ़ते हैं। [We read.]

Step 3, Make the past with जाना. कल मैं स्कूल गया। [Yesterday I went to school, a boy.] कल मैं स्कूल गई। [Yesterday I went to school, a girl.] हम बाज़ार गए। [We went to the market.] The ending shows gender and number.

Step 4, Make the future. कल मैं स्कूल जाऊँगा। [Tomorrow I will go to school, a boy.] कल मैं स्कूल जाऊँगी। [A girl.] हम बाग़ में खेलेंगे। [We will play in the garden.] Practise the same sentence in the three tenses.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says मैं स्कूल जाता है। Correction: मैं स्कूल जाता हूँ। because मैं goes with हूँ. Another says वह खेलती हूँ। Correction: वह खेलती है। because वह goes with है.

Step 6, Your turn: say what you do today, did yesterday and will do tomorrow with पढ़ना. Model answer: आज मैं किताब पढ़ता हूँ। कल मैंने किताब पढ़ी। कल मैं कहानी पढ़ूँगा। [Today I read a book. Yesterday I read a book. Tomorrow I will read a story.]

Step 1, Opposites (विलोम शब्द) mean the reverse. बड़ा–छोटा [big–small], ऊँचा–नीचा [high–low], गर्म–ठंडा [hot–cold], दिन–रात [day–night], आगे–पीछे [front–back]. Read each pair, then cover one word and say its opposite.

Step 2, More pairs. अंदर–बाहर [inside–outside], सच–झूठ [truth–lie], हँसना–रोना [to laugh–to cry], मीठा–कड़वा [sweet–bitter], नया–पुराना [new–old]. Make a pair card for each, with the word on one side and its opposite on the other.

Step 3, Use opposites in sentences. यह पहाड़ ऊँचा है और वह टीला नीचा है। [This mountain is high and that mound is low.] चाय गर्म है, पानी ठंडा है। [The tea is hot, the water is cold.] दिन में रोशनी होती है, रात में अँधेरा। [There is light in the day, darkness at night.]

Step 4, Match meaning with context. बच्चा अंदर है, बिल्ली बाहर है। [The child is inside, the cat is outside.] मीठा आम और कड़वा करेला [sweet mango and bitter gourd]. Use each pair in one sentence about a picture.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says the opposite of दिन is शाम. Correction: the opposite of दिन is रात; शाम is only part of the day. Adjectives must still agree: बड़ी मेज़ [big table] and छोटी कुर्सी [small chair], not बड़ा मेज़.

Step 6, Your turn: write the opposites of नया, अंदर and हँसना, then a sentence. Model answer: पुराना, बाहर, रोना। नया बस्ता पुराने बस्ते से अच्छा है। [Old, outside, to cry. The new bag is better than the old bag.]

Step 1, Read the passage. ذَهَبَتْ سَارَةُ مَعَ صَدِيقَتِهَا إِلَى مَكْتَبَةِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ. اسْتَعَارَتْ سَارَةُ كِتَابًا عَنِ الْحَيَوَانَاتِ، وَاخْتَارَتْ صَدِيقَتُهَا قِصَّةً عَنِ الْبَحْرِ. [Sara went with her friend to the school library on Thursday. Sara borrowed a book about animals, and her friend chose a story about the sea.]

Step 2, Read the rest. جَلَسَتَا مَعًا وَقَرَأَتَا بِهُدُوءٍ. فِي الْمَسَاءِ أَخْبَرَتْ سَارَةُ أُمَّهَا بِمَا تَعَلَّمَتْ. [The two sat together and read quietly. In the evening Sara told her mother what she had learned.] Underline the day, the place and the people.

Step 3, Answer direct questions. مَتَى ذَهَبَتْ سَارَةُ إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ؟ [When did Sara go to the library?] ذَهَبَتْ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ. [She went on Thursday.] مَاذَا اسْتَعَارَتْ؟ [What did she borrow?] اسْتَعَارَتْ كِتَابًا عَنِ الْحَيَوَانَاتِ. [She borrowed a book about animals.]

Step 4, Answer a thinking question. لِمَاذَا قَرَأَتَا بِهُدُوءٍ؟ [Why did they read quietly?] لِأَنَّهُمَا فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ. [Because they were in the library.] This reason is not written word for word, so use the clue كَانَتَا فِي مَكْتَبَةِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ [They were in the school library].

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes the whole passage as an answer to مَنْ اخْتَارَ قِصَّةً؟ [Who chose a story?]. Correction: choose the key sentence only, اخْتَارَتْ صَدِيقَةُ سَارَةَ قِصَّةً. [Sara's friend chose a story.] Short, exact answers score better.

Step 6, Your turn: give a title and answer: what did Sara do in the evening? Model answer: عُنْوَانٌ: زِيَارَةُ الْمَكْتَبَةِ [Title: A visit to the library]. أَخْبَرَتْ سَارَةُ أُمَّهَا بِمَا تَعَلَّمَتْ. [Sara told her mother what she learned.]

Step 1, Name sports. كُرَةُ الْقَدَمِ [football], كُرَةُ السَّلَّةِ [basketball], السِّبَاحَةُ [swimming], الْجَرْيُ [running], رُكُوبُ الدَّرَّاجَةِ [cycling]. Ask a partner: مَا رِيَاضَتُكَ الْمُفَضَّلَةُ؟ [What is your favourite sport?]

Step 2, Say what you do. أُمَارِسُ الرِّيَاضَةَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ. [I do sport three times a week.] أُحِبُّ السِّبَاحَةَ. [I like swimming.] أَجْرِي فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ. [I run in the park every morning.]

Step 3, Talk about healthy living. أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ كَثِيرًا. [I drink a lot of water.] الْفَوَاكِهُ وَالْخُضَارُ مُفِيدَةٌ لِلْجِسْمِ. [Fruit and vegetables are good for the body.] كَثْرَةُ الْحَلْوَى مُضِرَّةٌ. [Too many sweets are harmful.] Say each sentence slowly.

Step 4, Give advice with يَجِبُ أَنْ. يَجِبُ أَنْ أَنَامَ مُبَكِّرًا. [I must sleep early.] يَجِبُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ طَعَامًا صِحِّيًّا. [We must eat healthy food.] After أَنْ the present verb ends with a fatha sound: أَنَامَ، نَأْكُلَ.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says يَجِبُ أَنْ أَنَامُ مُبَكِّرًا. Correction: يَجِبُ أَنْ أَنَامَ مُبَكِّرًا, because the verb after أَنْ takes fatha. Another says أُحِبُّ السِّبَاحَةُ; use أُحِبُّ السِّبَاحَةَ.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences about your sport and a healthy habit. Model answer: أَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ. أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ كَثِيرًا. يَجِبُ أَنْ أَنَامَ مُبَكِّرًا. [I play football on Saturday. I drink a lot of water. I must sleep early.]

Step 1, A paragraph has a topic sentence, two or three details, and a closing sentence. Choose a topic: my school. First write the topic sentence: مَدْرَسَتِي مَكَانٌ جَمِيلٌ لِلتَّعَلُّمِ. [My school is a lovely place to learn.]

Step 2, Add details that support the topic. فِيهَا صُفُوفٌ وَاسِعَةٌ وَمَلْعَبٌ كَبِيرٌ. [It has spacious classrooms and a big playground.] أُحِبُّ الْمُعَلِّمِينَ لِأَنَّهُمْ يَشْرَحُونَ بِصَبْرٍ. [I like the teachers because they explain patiently.]

Step 3, Use linking words. وَ [and], لِأَنَّ [because], ثُمَّ [then], لِذَلِكَ [therefore]. Example: أَدْرُسُ بِجِدٍّ لِأَنِّي أُحِبُّ الْعِلْمَ. [I study hard because I love knowledge.] Add one linking word to each detail.

Step 4, Close the paragraph. لِذَلِكَ أَنَا سَعِيدٌ فِي مَدْرَسَتِي. [Therefore I am happy in my school.] Now read the paragraph from the topic sentence to the end and check that every sentence talks about school.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes a paragraph about school and then adds أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْبَحْرَ [I love the sea], which is off topic. Correction: delete it, or replace it with a school detail like فِي مَدْرَسَتِي مَكْتَبَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ [My school has a big library].

Step 6, Your turn: write a four-sentence paragraph on my family. Model answer: أُسْرَتِي صَغِيرَةٌ وَسَعِيدَةٌ. فِيهَا أَبِي وَأُمِّي وَأَخِي. نَأْكُلُ مَعًا كُلَّ مَسَاءٍ. لِذَلِكَ أُحِبُّ أُسْرَتِي. [My family is small and happy. It has my father, mother and brother. We eat together every evening. Therefore I love my family.]

Step 1, Describe the buildings. Mon école est grande et propre. [My school is big and clean.] Il y a vingt salles de classe, une cour, une bibliothèque et une cantine. [There are twenty classrooms, a yard, a library and a canteen.] Use il y a for there is and there are.

Step 2, Describe your class. Ma classe est lumineuse. [My class is bright.] Il y a vingt-cinq élèves. [There are twenty-five pupils.] Ma maîtresse est gentille. [My teacher is kind.] Notice maîtresse is feminine, so the adjective gentille ends with e.

Step 3, Say what you do and like. Ma matière préférée, c'est les maths. [My favourite subject is maths.] Je mange à la cantine. [I eat at the canteen.] À la récréation, je joue dans la cour. [At break I play in the yard.] Ask your partner the same.

Step 4, Dialogue. Sam : Comment est ton école ? [What is your school like?] Zoé : Elle est grande, avec une belle bibliothèque. [It is big with a lovely library.] Sam : Tu aimes ta classe ? [Do you like your class?] Zoé : Oui, j'adore ma classe ! [Yes, I love my class!]
Step 5, Fix errors. A child says Il y a vingt élève. Correction: Il y a vingt élèves, because the noun is plural. Another says ma école; use mon école, because mon is used before a vowel sound.

Step 6, Your turn: write four sentences about your school. Model answer: Mon école est petite mais jolie. Il y a douze classes et une grande cour. Ma matière préférée, c'est l'anglais. Je suis très content. [My school is small but pretty. There are twelve classes and a big yard. My favourite subject is English. I am very happy.]

Step 1, Verbs ending in er follow one pattern. parler [to speak]: je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent. Replace er with the endings e, es, e, ons, ez, ent. Example: Nous parlons français. [We speak French.]

Step 2, Verbs in ir like finir follow another. je finis, tu finis, il finit, nous finissons, vous finissez, ils finissent. Example: Elle finit ses devoirs. [She finishes her homework.] Nous finissons à quatre heures. [We finish at four o'clock.]

Step 3, Verbs in re like vendre [to sell]: je vends, tu vends, il vend, nous vendons, vous vendez, ils vendent. Example: Il vend des fruits. [He sells fruit.] The il form has no ending, only the stem vend.

Step 4, Practise a mixed dialogue. Maman : Qu'est-ce que tu fais ? [What are you doing?] Léa : Je finis mon exercice. [I am finishing my exercise.] Maman : Vous parlez de quoi ? [What are you talking about?] Léa : Nous parlons du voyage. [We are talking about the trip.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says nous parlez. Correction: nous parlons, because nous goes with ons. Another says je finit. Correction: je finis, because je takes s in the ir pattern. Also ils vend should be ils vendent.

Step 6, Your turn: conjugate habiter [to live] with je, nous and ils, then complete: Elles (finir) leur travail. Model answer: j'habite, nous habitons, ils habitent. Elles finissent leur travail. [I live, we live, they live. They finish their work.]

Step 1, To make a sentence negative put ne before the verb and pas after it. Je parle anglais. [I speak English.] Je ne parle pas anglais. [I do not speak English.] Before a vowel ne becomes n': Il n'aime pas le lait. [He does not like milk.]

Step 2, Learn definite and indefinite articles. le, la, l', les [the]; un, une, des [a, some]. Example: J'ai un chat et des poissons. [I have a cat and some fish.] Le chat est noir. [The cat is black.] Choose le for masculine, la for feminine.

Step 3, Learn partitive articles. du, de la, de l' [some], used for things you cannot count: Je mange du pain. [I eat some bread.] Je bois de l'eau. [I drink some water.] Elle mange de la soupe. [She eats some soup.]

Step 4, After a negative, un, une, des, du, de la change to de or d'. Je n'ai pas de frère. [I do not have a brother.] Je ne mange pas de pain. [I do not eat bread.] Il n'a pas d'amis. [He does not have friends.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says Je mange pas de viande. Correction: Je ne mange pas de viande, because ne is needed. Another says Je n'ai pas des amis. Correction: Je n'ai pas d'amis. A third says Je ne bois pas du lait; say pas de lait.

Step 6, Your turn: make these negative: Elle a un vélo. Nous buvons du thé. J'aime les carottes. Model answer: Elle n'a pas de vélo. Nous ne buvons pas de thé. Je n'aime pas les carottes. [She has no bike. We do not drink tea. I do not like carrots.]

Step 1, Learn nationalities with masculine and feminine. français, française [French]; italien, italienne [Italian]; indien, indienne [Indian]; marocain, marocaine [Moroccan]; anglais, anglaise [English]; espagnol, espagnole [Spanish]. They begin with a small letter.

Step 2, Say who you are. Je suis marocain. [I am Moroccan, a boy.] Je suis marocaine. [A girl.] Maria est italienne. [Maria is Italian.] Ils sont indiens. [They are Indian.] Elles sont françaises. [They are French, all girls.]

Step 3, Learn character adjectives. gentil, gentille [kind]; drôle [funny]; timide [shy]; courageux, courageuse [brave]; généreux, généreuse [generous]; sérieux, sérieuse [serious]. The ending eux changes to euse for a girl.

Step 4, Describe people. Maria est italienne. Elle est courageuse et généreuse. [Maria is Italian. She is brave and generous.] Karim est marocain. Il est timide mais drôle. [Karim is Moroccan. He is shy but funny.] Add parce que for a reason.

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says Elle est courageux. Correction: Elle est courageuse. Another says Il est indienne. Correction: Il est indien. A third writes Français with a capital; as an adjective it is français.

Step 6, Your turn: describe an Indian girl who is kind and serious. Model answer: Priya est indienne. Elle est gentille et sérieuse. Elle est aussi très drôle avec ses amis. [Priya is Indian. She is kind and serious. She is also very funny with her friends.]

Step 1, Read the first part of the story I wrote. गाँव के किनारे एक पुराना बरगद का पेड़ था। गर्मी में सब उसकी छाया में बैठते थे। [At the edge of the village there was an old banyan tree. In summer everyone sat in its shade.]

Step 2, Read the second part. एक दिन कुछ लोग पेड़ काटने आए। बच्चों ने मिलकर कहा, यह पेड़ हमारी छाया है। लोग रुक गए और पेड़ बच गया। [One day some men came to cut it. The children said together, This tree is our shade. The men stopped and the tree was saved.]

Step 3, Find the parts of the story. Setting: गाँव का किनारा [edge of the village]. Character: बच्चे और बरगद [the children and the banyan]. Problem: लोग पेड़ काटने आए [men came to cut the tree]. Solution: बच्चों ने उन्हें रोका [the children stopped them].

Step 4, Answer questions. सब गर्मी में कहाँ बैठते थे? [Where did everyone sit in summer?] सब पेड़ की छाया में बैठते थे। [Everyone sat in the shade of the tree.] पेड़ क्यों बच गया? [Why was the tree saved?] क्योंकि बच्चों ने लोगों को रोका। [Because the children stopped the men.]

Step 5, Find the moral. कहानी की सीख है कि पेड़ हमारे मित्र हैं और हमें उनकी रक्षा करनी चाहिए। [The moral is that trees are our friends and we should protect them.] Say the moral in your own words, starting with हमें.

Step 6, Fix an error. A child retells it as बरगद के पेड़ ने लोगों को रोका. Correction: the story says बच्चों ने लोगों को रोका। Check who did the action before you answer; a wrong doer changes the meaning of the story.

Step 7, Your turn: summarise the story in three sentences. Model answer: एक गाँव में पुराना बरगद का पेड़ था। कुछ लोग उसे काटने आए। बच्चों ने उन्हें रोका और पेड़ बच गया। [In a village there was an old banyan tree. Some men came to cut it. The children stopped them and the tree was saved.]

Step 1, A noun (संज्ञा) names something: रवि, किताब, दिल्ली. A pronoun (सर्वनाम) replaces a noun: मैं, तुम, वह, हम, यह, वे. An adjective (विशेषण) describes a noun: लंबा, सुंदर, मीठा. Find one of each in this sentence: रवि लंबा है।

Step 2, Use pronouns to avoid repeating. Without: मीना किताब पढ़ती है। मीना रोज़ पढ़ती है। Better: मीना किताब पढ़ती है। वह रोज़ पढ़ती है। [Meena reads a book. She reads every day.] मैं, तुम, वह are for I, you and he or she.

Step 3, Match adjectives to nouns. अच्छा लड़का [good boy], अच्छी लड़की [good girl], अच्छे लड़के [good boys]. Adjectives ending in आ change with the noun. सुंदर does not change: सुंदर लड़का, सुंदर लड़की, सुंदर लड़के.

Step 4, Use all three in a paragraph. रवि लंबा लड़का है। वह तेज़ दौड़ता है। मीना छोटी लड़की है। वह मीठा गाना गाती है। [Ravi is a tall boy. He runs fast. Meena is a small girl. She sings a sweet song.] Underline the nouns, circle the pronouns.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes अच्छी लड़का. Correction: अच्छा लड़का because लड़का is masculine. Another writes मैं और तुम खेलते है. Correction: हम खेलते हैं। or मैं और तुम खेलते हैं। because the doers are plural.

Step 6, Your turn: write two sentences about a girl and a boy using a pronoun and an adjective each. Model answer: सीमा होशियार लड़की है। वह रोज़ पढ़ती है। अमन बहादुर लड़का है। वह नहीं डरता। [Seema is a clever girl. She studies every day. Aman is a brave boy. He does not fear.]

Step 1, A prefix (उपसर्ग) comes before a word and changes its meaning. अ + सफल = असफल [unsuccessful], सु + गंध = सुगंध [fragrance], कु + संग = कुसंग [bad company], नि + डर = निडर [fearless]. Say each word and then its meaning.

Step 2, A suffix (प्रत्यय) comes after a word. बच्चा + पन = बचपन [childhood], दोस्त + ई = दोस्ती [friendship], सुंदर + ता = सुंदरता [beauty], दूध + वाला = दूधवाला [milkman]. Write each word and circle the added part.

Step 3, Use new words in sentences. उसने असफल होकर भी कोशिश नहीं छोड़ी। [Even after failing he did not give up.] फूलों की सुगंध बहुत अच्छी थी। [The fragrance of the flowers was very good.] बचपन की यादें मीठी होती हैं। [Childhood memories are sweet.]

Step 4, Build five new words. नि + र्भय = निर्भय [without fear], बे + घर = बेघर [homeless], अपना + पन = अपनापन [feeling of belonging], गरीब + ई = गरीबी [poverty], अ + न्याय = अन्याय [injustice]. Say each in a sentence.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes अ + आदर as अआदर. Correction: अनादर [disrespect], because before a vowel अ becomes अन्. Another writes सफलअ for unsuccessful; the prefix goes before: असफल.

Step 6, Your turn: build words with अ, सु and ई and use one. Model answer: अ + स्वस्थ = अस्वस्थ [unwell], सु + पुत्र = सुपुत्र [good son], खेत + ई = खेती [farming]. किसान खेती करते हैं। [Farmers do farming.]
Step 1, Synonyms (पर्यायवाची शब्द) mean the same. सूरज = सूर्य = दिनकर [sun], चाँद = चंद्रमा = शशि [moon], पानी = जल = नीर [water], फूल = पुष्प = सुमन [flower]. Read each row aloud.

Step 2, Use synonyms to vary a sentence. सूरज उगता है। सूर्य की किरणें खेत पर पड़ती हैं। [The sun rises. The sun's rays fall on the field.] Here सूरज and सूर्य mean the same, which avoids repeating one word.

Step 3, Antonyms (विलोम शब्द) mean the reverse. सुख–दुख [joy–sorrow], आशा–निराशा [hope–despair], मित्र–शत्रु [friend–enemy], जीत–हार [win–loss], आना–जाना [to come–to go]. Make flashcards and test a partner.

Step 4, Use both in one paragraph. मित्र सुख में साथ रहता है और दुख में भी। हार से निराशा नहीं, सीख मिलती है। [A friend stays with you in joy and in sorrow too. From a loss you get a lesson, not despair.] Underline each antonym pair.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says the opposite of बहादुर [brave] is मूर्ख [foolish]. Correction: the opposite of बहादुर is कायर [cowardly]. Opposites must be on the same idea; मूर्ख is the opposite of समझदार [wise].

Step 6, Your turn: give a synonym for पानी and an antonym for जीत, then write one sentence. Model answer: जल; हार. जल जीवन के लिए ज़रूरी है। [Water is necessary for life.] Both words are used correctly.

Step 1, Name birds and nature. الْعُصْفُورُ [sparrow], النَّسْرُ [eagle], الْحَمَامَةُ [dove], الْبُومَةُ [owl], الْغَابَةُ [forest], النَّهْرُ [river], الْجَبَلُ [mountain], الْهَوَاءُ النَّقِيُّ [clean air]. Group them into birds and places.

Step 2, Describe a bird. يَعِيشُ النَّسْرُ فِي الْجِبَالِ الْعَالِيَةِ وَيَطِيرُ عَالِيًا. [The eagle lives in high mountains and flies high.] الْبُومَةُ تَسْهَرُ فِي اللَّيْلِ. [The owl stays awake at night.] الطُّيُورُ جَمِيلَةٌ. [Birds are beautiful.]

Step 3, Talk about caring for the environment. نَزْرَعُ الْأَشْجَارَ. [We plant trees.] نُحَافِظُ عَلَى نَظَافَةِ النَّهْرِ. [We keep the river clean.] الْبِيئَةُ بَيْتُنَا الْكَبِيرُ. [The environment is our big home.] Give one reason with لِأَنَّ.

Step 4, Give advice with لَا for a ban. لَا تَرْمِ الْقُمَامَةَ فِي النَّهْرِ. [Do not throw rubbish in the river, to a boy.] لَا تَقْطَعِ الشَّجَرَةَ. [Do not cut the tree.] To a girl: لَا تَرْمِي الْقُمَامَةَ. Read both forms aloud.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says لَا تَرْمِي to a boy. Correction: for a boy say لَا تَرْمِ; the ending ـي is only for a girl. Another says الطُّيُورُ جَمِيلُونَ; birds are not people, so say الطُّيُورُ جَمِيلَةٌ.

Step 6, Your turn: write a short description of a forest and one piece of advice. Model answer: فِي الْغَابَةِ أَشْجَارٌ عَالِيَةٌ وَعَصَافِيرُ كَثِيرَةٌ. لَا تَقْطَعِ الْأَشْجَارَ، لِأَنَّهَا تُنَقِّي الْهَوَاءَ. [In the forest are tall trees and many birds. Do not cut the trees, because they clean the air.]

Step 1, A short letter has a greeting, a body and a closing. Begin: عَزِيزِي أَحْمَدُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ. [Dear Ahmad, peace and God's mercy upon you.] Put the date at the top and the sender's name at the end.

Step 2, Write an invitation body. يَسُرُّنِي أَنْ أَدْعُوَكَ إِلَى حَفْلِ عِيدِ مِيلَادِي يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الرَّابِعَةِ مَسَاءً فِي بَيْتِنَا. [I am pleased to invite you to my birthday party on Saturday at four o'clock in the afternoon at our house.] It gives the event, the day, the time and the place.

Step 3, Close the letter. أَنْتَظِرُكَ بِشَوْقٍ. [I await you eagerly.] صَدِيقُكَ، خَالِدٌ. [Your friend, Khalid.] A reply begins: شُكْرًا عَلَى دَعْوَتِكَ. سَأَحْضُرُ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ. [Thank you for your invitation. I will attend, God willing.]

Step 4, Check the grammar. After يَسُرُّنِي أَنْ the verb takes fatha: أَدْعُوَ. صَدِيقُكَ with ـكَ is used for a male reader, and صَدِيقَتُكِ is used when the writer is a girl writing to a girl: صَدِيقَتُكِ، سَلْمَى.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes the name first and the greeting last, and forgets the day. Correction: use the order greeting, invitation with day and time, closing, then name. Missing the day or place makes the invitation unclear.

Step 6, Your turn: write a short invitation to a school picnic. Model answer: عَزِيزَتِي نُورُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكِ. أَدْعُوكِ إِلَى رِحْلَةِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ. أَنْتَظِرُكِ. صَدِيقَتُكِ، لَيْلَى. [Dear Nour, peace be upon you. I invite you to the school trip on Thursday in the park. I await you. Your friend, Layla.]

Step 1, Read two lines I wrote. الْمَاءُ حَيَاةٌ فَلَا نُضَيِّعْهُ، وَالشَّجَرُ صَدِيقٌ فَلَا نَقْطَعْهُ. [Water is life, so we do not waste it; trees are friends, so we do not cut them.] Read slowly, once with a pause at the comma.

Step 2, Understand the words. الْمَاءُ [water], حَيَاةٌ [life], نُضَيِّعُ [we waste], الشَّجَرُ [trees], صَدِيقٌ [friend], نَقْطَعُ [we cut]. After لَا the verb ends in sukun: لَا نُضَيِّعْهُ، لَا نَقْطَعْهُ.
Step 3, Notice the rhyme. Both lines end in ـعْهُ: نُضَيِّعْهُ and نَقْطَعْهُ. This rhyme (قَافِيَةٌ) makes the lines easy to remember. Recite aloud, making the last sound the same each time.

Step 4, Explain the meaning. The poet says water and trees give life, so we should protect them. Write: يُرِيدُ الشَّاعِرُ أَنْ نُحَافِظَ عَلَى الْمَاءِ وَالشَّجَرِ. [The poet wants us to protect water and trees.] Add a saying: الْقِرَاءَةُ بَابٌ إِلَى الْعَالَمِ. [Reading is a door to the world.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student explains by repeating the poem word by word. Correction: explain the idea in your own words: the poem teaches us to care for nature. Another error is pausing in the middle of فَلَا نُضَيِّعْهُ; keep that phrase together.

Step 6, Your turn: explain in one sentence what الْقِرَاءَةُ بَابٌ إِلَى الْعَالَمِ means. Model answer: مَعْنَاهُ أَنَّنَا نَتَعَلَّمُ أَشْيَاءَ جَدِيدَةً وَنَعْرِفُ أَمَاكِنَ بَعِيدَةً عِنْدَمَا نَقْرَأُ. [It means we learn new things and know faraway places when we read.]

Step 1, Plan a one-minute talk with three parts. Opening: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، اسْمِي لَيْلَى، وَمَوْضُوعِي الْيَوْمَ عَنِ الْقِرَاءَةِ. [Peace be upon you, my name is Layla, and my topic today is reading.] Say it clearly and look at your audience.

Step 2, Give two points. أَوَّلًا، أُحِبُّ الْقِرَاءَةَ لِأَنَّهَا تُعَلِّمُنِي أَشْيَاءَ جَدِيدَةً. [First, I love reading because it teaches me new things.] ثَانِيًا، أَقْرَأُ كُلَّ مَسَاءٍ قَبْلَ النَّوْمِ. [Second, I read every evening before sleep.]

Step 3, Close the talk. وَفِي الْخِتَامِ، أَنْصَحُكُمْ بِقِرَاءَةِ كِتَابٍ كُلَّ أُسْبُوعٍ. شُكْرًا لِحُسْنِ اسْتِمَاعِكُمْ. [In conclusion, I advise you to read a book every week. Thank you for listening well.] Then ask: هَلْ مِنْ أَسْئِلَةٍ؟ [Are there any questions?]

Step 4, Practise a question and answer. زَمِيلٌ: مَا كِتَابُكِ الْمُفَضَّلُ؟ [What is your favourite book?] لَيْلَى: كِتَابٌ عَنِ الْحَيَوَانَاتِ. [A book about animals.] زَمِيلٌ: لِمَاذَا تُحِبِّينَهُ؟ [Why do you like it?] لَيْلَى: لِأَنَّ صُوَرَهُ جَمِيلَةٌ. [Because its pictures are beautiful.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A speaker reads a paper without looking up, speaks too fast and finishes without a closing. Correction: pause after each point, look at the audience, and end with وَفِي الْخِتَامِ and شُكْرًا. Say أَوَّلًا and ثَانِيًا clearly.

Step 6, Your turn: write and say a four-sentence talk about my favourite sport. Model answer: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، مَوْضُوعِي كُرَةُ الْقَدَمِ. أُحِبُّهَا لِأَنَّهَا تُقَوِّي الْجِسْمَ. أَلْعَبُ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي كُلَّ سَبْتٍ. شُكْرًا لِحُسْنِ اسْتِمَاعِكُمْ. [Peace be upon you, my topic is football. I love it because it strengthens the body. I play with my friends every Saturday. Thank you for listening.]

Step 1, Read the four lines I wrote. नदी चली पर्वत से, गाती हुई, सागर से मिलने, इठलाती हुई। कहती है मुझसे, चलते रहना, हर बाधा से आगे बढ़ते रहना। [The river set off from the mountain, singing, to meet the sea, swaying. It tells me, keep moving, go forward past every obstacle.]

Step 2, Understand the words. पर्वत [mountain], सागर [sea], इठलाती [swaying playfully], बाधा [obstacle], आगे बढ़ना [to move forward]. Write each meaning in your notebook and read the lines again with the meanings in mind.

Step 3, Explain the lines. The first two lines describe the river's journey. The last two lines give the river's message: never stop, whatever blocks you. Write: कवि नदी के माध्यम से हमें निरंतर चलने की प्रेरणा देता है। [Through the river the poet inspires us to keep moving.]
