Step 4, Name the poetic devices. The river sings and speaks like a person; this is personification (मानवीकरण). The sounds हुई and हुई repeat at line ends, and रहना repeats too, creating rhythm. Read the poem aloud, stressing the rhyming ends.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student says the poem is only about a river travelling. Correction: the poem also carries a message about perseverance, so explain the central idea: हर बाधा के बाद भी हमें आगे बढ़ना चाहिए। [We should keep going even after every obstacle.]

Step 6, Your turn: say what the river wants to meet and what it teaches. Model answer: नदी सागर से मिलना चाहती है। वह सिखाती है कि हमें बाधाओं से रुकना नहीं चाहिए। [The river wants to meet the sea. It teaches that we should not stop because of obstacles.]

Step 1, Read the story I wrote. كَانَ فِي قَرْيَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ صَبِيٌّ اسْمُهُ يُوسُفُ يَخَافُ مِنَ الظَّلَامِ. فِي لَيْلَةٍ انْقَطَعَ النُّورُ، فَأَشْعَلَ شَمْعَةً وَسَاعَدَ جَارَتَهُ الْعَجُوزَ. [In a small village there was a boy named Yusuf who feared the dark. One night the electricity went out, so he lit a candle and helped his old neighbour.]

Step 2, Read the ending. عِنْدَهَا عَرَفَ أَنَّ الشَّجَاعَةَ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ الْخَيْرَ رَغْمَ الْخَوْفِ. [Then he knew that courage is to do good in spite of fear.] Underline the lesson sentence, which tells you what the story teaches.

Step 3, List the story elements. الشَّخْصِيَّاتُ [characters]: يُوسُفُ وَالْجَارَةُ. الْمَكَانُ [place]: قَرْيَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ. الْمُشْكِلَةُ [problem]: الْخَوْفُ مِنَ الظَّلَامِ. الْحَلُّ [solution]: شَمْعَةٌ وَمُسَاعَدَةٌ. الْعِبْرَةُ [lesson]: الشَّجَاعَةُ فِعْلُ الْخَيْرِ. Fill in each from the text.

Step 4, Write a three-sentence summary. يُحْكَى عَنْ صَبِيٍّ يَخَافُ مِنَ الظَّلَامِ. فِي لَيْلَةٍ انْقَطَعَ النُّورُ فَسَاعَدَ جَارَتَهُ بِشَمْعَةٍ. تَعَلَّمَ أَنَّ الشَّجَاعَةَ فِعْلُ الْخَيْرِ. [It is told of a boy who feared the dark. One night, when the light went out, he helped his neighbour with a candle. He learned that courage is doing good.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student retells every detail, including the village size, and adds an opinion. Correction: a summary keeps only the main events in your own words, in the past tense, and leaves out opinions. Aim for about a third of the text.

Step 6, Your turn: write two sentences on why the neighbour needed Yusuf and what he learned. Model answer: كَانَتِ الْجَارَةُ الْعَجُوزُ تَحْتَاجُ إِلَى النُّورِ. تَعَلَّمَ يُوسُفُ أَنْ يَتَغَلَّبَ عَلَى خَوْفِهِ. [The old neighbour needed light. Yusuf learned to overcome his fear.]

Step 1, Learn the past forms of كَتَبَ [to write]. كَتَبْتُ [I wrote], كَتَبْتَ [you wrote, m], كَتَبْتِ [you wrote, f], كَتَبَ [he wrote], كَتَبَتْ [she wrote], كَتَبْنَا [we wrote]. The endings are added to the stem كَتَب.

Step 2, Learn the present forms. أَكْتُبُ [I write], تَكْتُبُ [you write, m], تَكْتُبِينَ [you write, f], يَكْتُبُ [he writes], تَكْتُبُ [she writes], نَكْتُبُ [we write]. The prefixes أ ت ي ن show the person.

Step 3, Use time words. أَمْسِ كَتَبْتُ رِسَالَةً. [Yesterday I wrote a letter.] الْآنَ أَكْتُبُ وَاجِبِي. [Now I am writing my homework.] غَدًا سَأَكْتُبُ مَقَالًا. [Tomorrow I will write an essay.] Add سَـ before the present verb to make it future.

Step 4, Try another verb, ذَهَبَ [to go]. ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ أَمْسِ. [We went to the library yesterday.] هِيَ تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. [She goes to school every day.] Say the past and present of both verbs for three persons.

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says هِيَ كَتَبَ الدَّرْسَ. Correction: هِيَ كَتَبَتِ الدَّرْسَ, because she needs the feminine ending ـَتْ. Another says نَحْنُ ذَهَبْتُ; correction: نَحْنُ ذَهَبْنَا, because we ends with ـنَا.

Step 6, Your turn: write one past and one present sentence with the verb قَرَأَ [to read]. Model answer: أَمْسِ قَرَأْتُ قِصَّةً. الْآنَ أَقْرَأُ كِتَابًا. [Yesterday I read a story. Now I am reading a book.] Check that قَرَأْتُ ends in تُ for I.

Step 1, Open a call politely. أَلُو، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. [Hello, peace be upon you.] هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ مَعَ سَلْمَى؟ [May I speak with Salma?] The reply is وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. مَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ؟ [And upon you peace. Who is speaking?]

Step 2, Say who you are. أَنَا خَالِدٌ، زَمِيلُهَا فِي الصَّفِّ. [I am Khalid, her classmate.] نَعَمْ، لَحْظَةً مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. [Yes, one moment please.] عُذْرًا، سَلْمَى غَيْرُ مَوْجُودَةٍ الْآنَ. [Sorry, Salma is not here now.]

Step 3, Leave a message. هَلْ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَتْرُكَ رِسَالَةً؟ [Do you want to leave a message?] نَعَمْ، أَخْبِرْهَا أَنَّ الِاجْتِمَاعَ غَدًا. [Yes, tell her the meeting is tomorrow.] حَسَنًا، سَأُخْبِرُهَا. [Fine, I will tell her.]

Step 4, Close the call. شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ. [Thank you very much. Goodbye.] If you dialled wrongly: عُذْرًا، الرَّقْمُ خَطَأٌ. [Sorry, wrong number.] Act out the full call with a partner, then swap roles.

Step 5, Fix an error. A caller says هَلْ تَتْرُكُ رِسَالَةً؟ with no أَنْ. Correction: هَلْ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَتْرُكَ رِسَالَةً؟ because after أَنْ the verb takes fatha. Also never hang up without saying مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ.

Step 6, Your turn: phone a friend to ask about homework. Model answer: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَنَا نُورُ. هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَ عَنِ الْوَاجِبِ؟ شُكْرًا. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ. [Peace be upon you. I am Nour. May I ask about the homework? Thank you. Goodbye.]

Step 1, A description has three parts: appearance, character, example. For a person write: جَدِّي رَجُلٌ طَوِيلُ الْقَامَةِ، أَبْيَضُ الشَّعْرِ. [My grandfather is a tall man with white hair.] Notice طَوِيلُ الْقَامَةِ [tall of stature] is a common phrase.

Step 2, Add character. هُوَ هَادِئٌ وَكَرِيمٌ. [He is calm and generous.] يَبْتَسِمُ دَائِمًا. [He always smiles.] Choose adjectives that agree: for a woman say جَدَّتِي امْرَأَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ [My grandmother is a kind woman].

Step 3, Give an example that proves the character. فِي كُلِّ جُمْعَةٍ يُوزِّعُ الْحَلْوَى عَلَى الْأَطْفَالِ. [Every Friday he gives out sweets to the children.] Connect with لِذَلِكَ [therefore]: لِذَلِكَ يُحِبُّهُ الْجَمِيعُ. [Therefore everyone loves him.]

Step 4, Describe a place. مَدِينَتِي سَاحِلِيَّةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ. شَوَارِعُهَا نَظِيفَةٌ وَبُيُوتُهَا بَيْضَاءُ. يَبْدُو الْبَحْرُ كَأَنَّهُ مِرْآةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ. [My town is a small coastal town. Its streets are clean and its houses white. The sea looks like a big mirror.] The word كَأَنَّ makes a simile.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes a list: طَوِيلٌ، كَرِيمٌ، هَادِئٌ. Correction: join the ideas in sentences and give an example, as in جَدِّي كَرِيمٌ لِأَنَّهُ يُسَاعِدُ الْفُقَرَاءَ [My grandfather is generous because he helps the poor]. Also agree adjectives with the noun.

Step 6, Your turn: describe your mother in three sentences. Model answer: أُمِّي امْرَأَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ وَهَادِئَةٌ. تَعْمَلُ بِجِدٍّ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. لِذَلِكَ أُحِبُّهَا كَثِيرًا. [My mother is a beautiful, calm woman. She works hard every day. Therefore I love her very much.]

Step 1, Describe the town in general. Ma ville est petite et calme. [My town is small and quiet.] Elle est au bord de la mer. [It is by the sea.] Il y a une place, un marché, un parc et une gare. [There is a square, a market, a park and a station.]

Step 2, Say where things are with prepositions. Le marché est en face de la mairie. [The market is opposite the town hall.] Le parc est à côté de l'école. [The park is next to the school.] La gare est près du centre mais loin de la plage. [The station is near the centre but far from the beach.]

Step 3, Give directions. Pour aller à la gare, allez tout droit. [To go to the station, go straight on.] Tournez à gauche, puis à droite. [Turn left, then right.] C'est à cinq minutes à pied. [It is five minutes on foot.] Use the vous form to be polite.

Step 4, Dialogue with a visitor. Touriste : Excusez-moi, où est la mairie ? [Excuse me, where is the town hall?] Vous : Elle est en face du marché. [It is opposite the market.] Touriste : Merci beaucoup ! [Thank you very much!] Vous : De rien. [You are welcome.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says à côté la gare. Correction: à côté de la gare. Another says Il y a beaucoup des magasins. Correction: Il y a beaucoup de magasins. Also de + le becomes du: près du parc, not près de le parc.

Step 6, Your turn: describe your town with two places and one direction. Model answer: Ma ville est animée. Il y a un marché en face de la gare. Pour aller à l'école, tournez à droite. [My town is lively. There is a market opposite the station. To go to school, turn right.]

Step 1, Adjectives agree with the noun. grand, grande, grands, grandes [tall or big]. Le parc est grand. La place est grande. Les parcs sont grands. Les places sont grandes. Add e for feminine and s for plural.

Step 2, Learn an irregular adjective. beau [beautiful, masculine], belle [feminine], beaux [masculine plural], belles [feminine plural]. Un beau jardin. Une belle maison. De beaux arbres. De belles fleurs. Say each phrase aloud.

Step 3, Express cause with parce que. J'aime ma ville parce qu'elle est calme. [I like my town because it is quiet.] Before a vowel, que becomes qu'. Also use car [for, because]: Je reste ici, car j'aime la mer. [I stay here, as I love the sea.]

Step 4, Use à cause de with a noun. Nous restons à la maison à cause de la pluie. [We stay at home because of the rain.] Combine: Les rues sont belles parce que les habitants plantent des fleurs. [The streets are beautiful because the inhabitants plant flowers.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says Les maisons sont beau. Correction: Les maisons sont belles. Another says à cause que. Correction: parce que before a clause, à cause de before a noun. A third says parce que elle; use parce qu'elle.

Step 6, Your turn: write one sentence about the beautiful gardens and one with because of the wind. Model answer: Les jardins sont beaux parce que les gens les aiment. Nous ne sortons pas à cause du vent. [The gardens are beautiful because people love them. We do not go out because of the wind.]

Step 1, Read the passage I wrote. हमारे स्कूल के पीछे एक छोटा-सा बगीचा है। हर सप्ताह सातवीं कक्षा के विद्यार्थी वहाँ पौधों को पानी देते हैं और सूखे पत्ते हटाते हैं। [Behind our school there is a small garden. Every week seventh-grade students water the plants there and remove dry leaves.]

Step 2, Read the rest. पिछले महीने लगाए गए टमाटर अब पकने लगे हैं। इस काम से विद्यार्थियों ने मेहनत और ज़िम्मेदारी का महत्त्व सीखा। [Tomatoes planted last month have now started ripening. Through this work the students learned the value of hard work and responsibility.]

Step 3, Find the main idea and key points. Main idea: बगीचे की देखभाल से बच्चे ज़िम्मेदारी सीखते हैं [Caring for the garden teaches children responsibility]. Key points: पानी देना, पत्ते हटाना, टमाटर पकना. Mark these in the passage.

Step 4, Write a summary. स्कूल के बगीचे की देखभाल सातवीं कक्षा के विद्यार्थी करते हैं। टमाटर पकने लगे हैं और बच्चों ने मेहनत व ज़िम्मेदारी सीखी। [Seventh-grade students look after the school garden. The tomatoes are ripening and the children learned hard work and responsibility.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes a summary as long as the passage and adds मुझे बगीचा बहुत अच्छा लगता है [I like the garden very much]. Correction: a summary is about one third as long, in your own words, with no opinion.

Step 6, Your turn: answer what the students do every week and what they learned. Model answer: विद्यार्थी हर सप्ताह पौधों को पानी देते हैं और सूखे पत्ते हटाते हैं। उन्होंने मेहनत और ज़िम्मेदारी का महत्त्व सीखा। [Students water the plants and remove dry leaves every week. They learned the value of hard work and responsibility.]

Step 1, Case (कारक) shows the role of a noun using small words: ने, को, से, के लिए, का/की/के, में, पर. Examples: राम ने आम खाया। [Ram ate a mango.] माँ ने बच्चे को दूध दिया। [Mother gave milk to the child.] मैं पेंसिल से लिखता हूँ। [I write with a pencil.]

Step 2, More cases. पेड़ से पत्ता गिरा। [A leaf fell from the tree.] सीता का भाई स्कूल में है। [Seeta's brother is in school.] मेज़ पर किताब है। [There is a book on the table.] Name each word and its role: का shows relation, में shows place.

Step 3, Learn sandhi (joining of sounds). विद्या + आलय = विद्यालय [school], पुस्तक + आलय = पुस्तकालय [library], सूर्य + उदय = सूर्योदय [sunrise], महा + उत्सव = महोत्सव [grand festival]. Say each pair, then the joined word.

Step 4, A consonant sandhi: सत् + जन = सज्जन [good person], उत् + नति = उन्नति [progress]. Break the word the other way too: विद्यालय = विद्या + आलय. Then find parts of a sentence: राम (doer) आम (object) खाता है (action).

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes मोहन ने रोटी खाया। Correction: मोहन ने रोटी खाई। because with ने the verb agrees with the object रोटी, which is feminine. Also write पुस्तक + आलय as पुस्तकालय, not पुस्तकआलय.

Step 6, Your turn: write a sentence with ने and का, then join देव + आलय. Model answer: सीता ने भाई का बस्ता उठाया। देव + आलय = देवालय [temple]. [Seeta lifted her brother's bag.] Check ने with the past verb.

Step 1, Read the lines I wrote. दीपक जला है अँधेरी रात में, कहता है जग से, मैं अकेला नहीं हूँ। हर किरण मेरी दूसरों की राह है, जो बाँटता है उजाला, वही महान है। [A lamp burns in the dark night, saying, I am not alone. Each ray is another's path; one who shares light is great.]

Step 2, Understand the words. दीपक [lamp], जग [world], किरण [ray], राह [path], उजाला [light], महान [great]. Write each meaning and read again. Notice the poem has no strict rhyme, so it is read by its meaning and rhythm.

Step 3, Find the symbols. The lamp stands for a helpful person; the dark night stands for difficulty or ignorance; light stands for kindness and knowledge. Write: दीपक उस व्यक्ति का प्रतीक है जो दूसरों की मदद करता है। [The lamp is a symbol of a person who helps others.]

Step 4, Explain the message. कवि कहता है कि सच्ची महानता अपना सुख बाँटने में है। [The poet says true greatness lies in sharing one's gifts.] Point to the last line as the key line. Identify personification: the lamp speaks like a person.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student explains only that a lamp burns at night. Correction: that is the literal meaning; add the deeper meaning: the lamp shows a person who gives help, so the poem is about sharing and kindness.

Step 6, Your turn: say what the dark night stands for and what the poem teaches. Model answer: अँधेरी रात मुश्किल समय का प्रतीक है। कविता सिखाती है कि हमें दूसरों के जीवन में उजाला बाँटना चाहिए। [The dark night stands for a difficult time. The poem teaches that we should share light in the lives of others.]

Step 1, Read the fable I wrote. كَانَ طَاوُوسٌ يَسْخَرُ مِنْ عُصْفُورٍ بِرِيشِهِ الْبَسِيطِ. جَاءَتْ عَاصِفَةٌ، فَثَقُلَ ذَيْلُ الطَّاوُوسِ بِالْمَاءِ وَلَمْ يَسْتَطِعِ الطَّيَرَانَ. [A peacock used to mock a sparrow for its plain feathers. A storm came, and the peacock's tail grew heavy with water so he could not fly.]

Step 2, Read the ending. أَمَّا الْعُصْفُورُ فَطَارَ إِلَى عُشِّهِ وَنَجَا. ثُمَّ عَادَ وَأَرْشَدَ الطَّاوُوسَ إِلَى مَأْوًى. [As for the sparrow, he flew to his nest and was safe. Then he came back and guided the peacock to shelter.] Notice أَمَّا ... فَ shows contrast.

Step 3, State the moral. الْعِبْرَةُ: لَا نَسْخَرُ مِنَ الْآخَرِينَ، فَالْقِيمَةُ بِالْفِعْلِ لَا بِالْمَظْهَرِ. [The moral: we do not mock others, for worth is in deeds, not looks.] Link it to the story: the peacock's beauty did not help him.

Step 4, Retell with connectors. فِي الْبِدَايَةِ سَخِرَ الطَّاوُوسُ مِنَ الْعُصْفُورِ. ثُمَّ جَاءَتِ الْعَاصِفَةُ. لَكِنَّ الْعُصْفُورَ نَجَا وَسَاعَدَ الطَّاوُوسَ. وَفِي النِّهَايَةِ تَعَلَّمَ الطَّاوُوسُ التَّوَاضُعَ. [At first the peacock mocked. Then the storm came. But the sparrow escaped and helped. In the end the peacock learned humility.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student states the moral as الطَّاوُوسُ جَمِيلٌ. Correction: that is a fact, not a moral; a moral is a lesson for readers, such as لَا نَغْتَرُّ بِمَظْهَرِنَا [we should not be proud of our looks]. Also keep the past tense when retelling.

Step 6, Your turn: write a three-sentence retelling with the moral. Model answer: سَخِرَ طَاوُوسٌ مِنْ عُصْفُورٍ. لَكِنَّ الْعَاصِفَةَ أَوْقَعَتِ الطَّاوُوسَ فِي مَأْزِقٍ فَسَاعَدَهُ الْعُصْفُورُ. الْعِبْرَةُ: التَّوَاضُعُ أَجْمَلُ مِنَ الْمَظْهَرِ. [A peacock mocked a sparrow. But the storm put the peacock in trouble and the sparrow helped him. Moral: humility is better than looks.]

Step 1, Attached pronouns show possession: كِتَابِي [my book], كِتَابُكَ [your book, m], كِتَابُكِ [your book, f], كِتَابُهُ [his book], كِتَابُهَا [her book], كِتَابُنَا [our book], كِتَابُهُمْ [their book]. Say each with the noun كِتَابٌ.

Step 2, Detached pronouns stand alone: أَنَا [I], أَنْتَ [you, m], أَنْتِ [you, f], هُوَ [he], هِيَ [she], نَحْنُ [we], أَنْتُمْ [you, pl], هُمْ [they, m], هُنَّ [they, f]. Use them: هِيَ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ. [She is hardworking.]

Step 3, Verb and subject agreement. When the verb comes first it stays singular and matches only the gender: ذَهَبَ الطُّلَّابُ [The students went], ذَهَبَتِ الطَّالِبَاتُ [The female students went]. When the pronoun comes first, the verb agrees fully: هُمْ ذَهَبُوا [They went].

Step 4, Adjective agreement. طَالِبَةٌ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ [a hardworking girl student], طُلَّابٌ مُجْتَهِدُونَ [hardworking students], كُتُبٌ جَدِيدَةٌ [new books]. A plural of a non-person takes a feminine singular adjective: جَدِيدَةٌ, not جَدِيدُونَ.

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says ذَهَبُوا الطُّلَّابُ. Correction: ذَهَبَ الطُّلَّابُ, because the verb precedes the subject. Another says الْكُتُبُ جَدِيدُونَ. Correction: الْكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ. A third says كِتَابُهُ for a girl's book; use كِتَابُهَا.

Step 6, Your turn: translate She is hardworking and her books are new. Model answer: هِيَ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ وَكُتُبُهَا جَدِيدَةٌ. [She is hardworking and her books are new.] Check that مُجْتَهِدَةٌ is feminine and كُتُبُهَا uses the her pronoun.

Step 1, Read the lines I wrote. لِلْوَطَنِ فِي الْقَلْبِ مَكَانْ، نَحْمِيهِ بِالْعِلْمِ وَالْإِيمَانْ. نَزْرَعُ الْخَيْرَ فِي كُلِّ مَكَانْ، فَتُزْهِرُ الدُّنْيَا بِلَا أَحْزَانْ. [The homeland has a place in the heart; we protect it with knowledge and faith. We plant good everywhere, so the world blooms without sorrows.]

Step 2, Understand the vocabulary. الْوَطَنُ [homeland], نَحْمِي [we protect], الْعِلْمُ [knowledge], الْإِيمَانُ [faith], نَزْرَعُ [we plant], تُزْهِرُ [blooms], أَحْزَانٌ [sorrows]. Write the meaning above each word.

Step 3, Identify rhyme and rhythm. Each line ends in ـَانْ: مَكَانْ، الْإِيمَانْ، مَكَانْ، أَحْزَانْ. This end rhyme is called قَافِيَةٌ. Read the lines aloud, keeping the same beat and lengthening the final sound.

Step 4, Explain the images and message. Planting good (نَزْرَعُ الْخَيْرَ) is a metaphor: kindness is a seed that grows into a better world. Write: يَدْعُو الشَّاعِرُ إِلَى حُبِّ الْوَطَنِ وَنَشْرِ الْخَيْرِ. [The poet calls for love of the homeland and spreading good.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student says the poem is about farming. Correction: نَزْرَعُ is figurative; the poem is about loving the homeland and doing good. Another student reads it without the rhyme sound; keep the ـَانْ ending clear.

Step 6, Your turn: explain the line فَتُزْهِرُ الدُّنْيَا بِلَا أَحْزَانْ. Model answer: تَعْنِي أَنَّ الْخَيْرَ إِذَا انْتَشَرَ جَعَلَ الْعَالَمَ سَعِيدًا وَخَالِيًا مِنَ الْحُزْنِ. [It means that when good spreads, it makes the world happy and free of sorrow.]

Step 1, A short speech has an opening, arguments and a closing. Topic: using mobile phones in class. Open: حَضَرَاتِ الزُّمَلَاءِ وَالزَّمِيلَاتِ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. مَوْضُوعُنَا الْيَوْمَ الْهَاتِفُ الْمَحْمُولُ فِي الصَّفِّ. [Dear colleagues, peace be upon you. Our topic today is the mobile phone in class.]

Step 2, State your position and first argument. أَنَا مَعَ مَنْعِ الْهَاتِفِ فِي الصَّفِّ لِأَنَّهُ يُشَتِّتُ الِانْتِبَاهَ. [I am for banning the phone in class because it distracts attention.] بِالْإِضَافَةِ إِلَى ذَلِكَ، يَقِلُّ الْحِوَارُ بَيْنَ الطُّلَّابِ. [In addition, discussion among students decreases.]

Step 3, Answer the other side. يَقُولُ الْبَعْضُ إِنَّ الْهَاتِفَ يُفِيدُ فِي الْبَحْثِ. وَلَكِنْ يُمْكِنُ اسْتِعْمَالُهُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ تَحْتَ إِشْرَافِ الْمُعَلِّمِ. [Some say the phone helps with research. But it can be used in the library under teacher supervision.]

Step 4, Close strongly. فِي الْخِتَامِ، لِنَجْعَلِ الصَّفَّ مَكَانًا لِلتَّرْكِيزِ وَالْحِوَارِ. شُكْرًا لِحُسْنِ إِصْغَائِكُمْ. [In conclusion, let us make the class a place of focus and discussion. Thank you for your attention.] Practise with a timer: one minute.

Step 5, Fix an error. A speaker says only أَنَا لَا أُحِبُّ الْهَاتِفَ [I do not like the phone], which is a feeling, not an argument. Correction: give a reason with لِأَنَّ and an example, then answer the opposing view with وَلَكِنْ.

Step 6, Your turn: write a three-sentence argument for longer school breaks. Model answer: أَنَا مَعَ زِيَادَةِ وَقْتِ الاِسْتِرَاحَةِ لِأَنَّهَا تُنَشِّطُ الْعَقْلَ. بِالْإِضَافَةِ إِلَى ذَلِكَ، يَلْعَبُ الطُّلَّابُ مَعًا. لِذَلِكَ أَرْجُو مِنْكُمْ تَأْيِيدَ الْفِكْرَةِ. [I support longer breaks because they refresh the mind. In addition, students play together. So I ask you to support the idea.]

Step 1, The passé composé talks about finished actions. Form: avoir in the present plus the past participle. J'ai mangé [I ate], tu as fini [you finished], nous avons joué [we played]. Hier, j'ai joué au foot. [Yesterday I played football.]

Step 2, Some verbs use être: aller, arriver, partir, venir, entrer. Je suis allé au marché. [I went to the market, a boy.] Elle est arrivée à huit heures. [She arrived at eight.] With être the participle agrees: allé, allée, allés, allées.

Step 3, The near future uses aller plus the infinitive. Je vais manger. [I am going to eat.] Nous allons jouer demain. [We are going to play tomorrow.] The simple future adds endings to the infinitive: je mangerai, tu finiras, nous jouerons. [I will eat, you will finish, we will play.]

Step 4, Dialogue. Sara : Qu'est-ce que tu as fait hier ? [What did you do yesterday?] Ali : J'ai regardé un film. [I watched a film.] Sara : Et demain ? [And tomorrow?] Ali : Demain, je jouerai au tennis. [Tomorrow I will play tennis.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says j'ai allé. Correction: je suis allé, because aller takes être. Another says je vais mangé. Correction: je vais manger, with the infinitive. A third says elle est allé; correction: elle est allée.

Step 6, Your turn: write yesterday, now and tomorrow with finir. Model answer: Hier, j'ai fini mes devoirs. Aujourd'hui, je finis mon livre. Demain, je finirai mon projet. [Yesterday I finished my homework. Today I finish my book. Tomorrow I will finish my project.]

Step 1, Learn pronominal verbs for the morning. je me réveille [I wake up], je me lève [I get up], je me lave [I wash], je m'habille [I get dressed]. The me stays before the verb. Say: Je me réveille à sept heures. [I wake up at seven.]

Step 2, Add other routine verbs. Je prends le petit déjeuner. [I have breakfast.] Je vais à l'école à huit heures et demie. [I go to school at half past eight.] Je mange à midi. [I eat at noon.] Je rentre à la maison à cinq heures. [I go home at five.]

Step 3, Write the evening. Je fais mes devoirs. [I do my homework.] Je dîne avec ma famille. [I have dinner with my family.] Je me couche à neuf heures. [I go to bed at nine.] Use d'abord, ensuite, puis, enfin for order.

Step 4, Connect in a short paragraph. D'abord, je me réveille à sept heures. Ensuite, je prends le petit déjeuner. Puis je vais à l'école. Enfin, le soir, je me couche tôt. [First I wake up at seven. Then I have breakfast. Then I go to school. Finally in the evening I go to bed early.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says je réveille à sept heure. Correction: je me réveille à sept heures. Another writes tu te lèves with je: je te lève; correction: je me lève. Also keep the s on heures when the number is more than one.

Step 6, Your turn: write four sentences about your day with times. Model answer: Je me lève à sept heures. Je vais à l'école à huit heures. Je rentre à quatre heures. Je me couche à dix heures. [I get up at seven. I go to school at eight. I come home at four. I go to bed at ten.]

Step 1, Read the passage. रेखा रोज़ सुबह पाँच बजे उठकर अपने पिता के साथ खेत पर जाती थी। वहाँ वह गायों को चारा देती और फिर स्कूल के लिए तैयार होती थी। [Rekha rose at five each morning and went to the field with her father. There she fed the cows, then got ready for school.]

Step 2, Read the second part. उसके शिक्षक उसकी मेहनत देखकर प्रसन्न थे। उन्होंने उसे पुस्तकालय की सदस्यता दिलवाई। अब रेखा खाली समय में कहानियाँ पढ़ती है। [Her teachers were pleased to see her hard work. They got her a library membership. Now Rekha reads stories in her free time.]

Step 3, Read the questions first, then reread the passage. Answer literal questions in full: रेखा कब उठती थी? [When did Rekha get up?] रेखा सुबह पाँच बजे उठती थी। [Rekha got up at five in the morning.]

Step 4, Answer vocabulary and inference. प्रसन्न का अर्थ क्या है? [What does प्रसन्न mean?] इसका अर्थ है खुश। [It means happy.] शिक्षक प्रसन्न क्यों थे? [Why were the teachers pleased?] क्योंकि रेखा मेहनती थी। [Because Rekha was hardworking.] Add a suitable title: मेहनती रेखा.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes रेखा देर से उठती थी। Correction: the passage says she got up at five in the morning, so the answer is रेखा सुबह पाँच बजे उठती थी। Always check the text, never answer from memory or guess.

Step 6, Your turn: answer what Rekha does now and give a one-word quality. Model answer: अब रेखा खाली समय में कहानियाँ पढ़ती है। उसका गुण है मेहनत। [Now Rekha reads stories in her free time. Her quality is hard work.]

Step 1, An idiom (मुहावरा) has a special meaning, not the literal one. आँखों का तारा [apple of the eye, a dearly loved person], नाक में दम करना [to pester someone], हाथ मलना [to regret], दाँतों तले उँगली दबाना [to be astonished]. Learn each meaning.

Step 2, Use idioms in sentences. नन्ही गुड़िया पूरे घर की आँखों का तारा है। [The little girl is the apple of the whole family's eye.] शरारती बंदर ने सबकी नाक में दम कर दिया। [The naughty monkey pestered everyone.] Replace the idiom with its meaning to check.

Step 3, Learn a proverb (कहावत): ऊँट के मुँह में जीरा means a very small amount compared with the need. Use: दो रोटियाँ पाँच लोगों के लिए ऊँट के मुँह में जीरा हैं। [Two rotis for five people is a drop in the ocean.]

Step 4, Use idioms in a short paragraph. परीक्षा में पहली आने पर रानी के माता-पिता खुशी से झूम उठे। अध्यापक ने उसका काम देखा तो दाँतों तले उँगली दबा ली। [Her parents were thrilled when Rani came first in the exam. The teacher was astonished when he saw her work.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes the literal meaning of नाक में दम करना as to put breath in the nose. Correction: it means to trouble someone constantly. Always give the figurative meaning of an idiom.

Step 6, Your turn: write one sentence with हाथ मलना and one with आँखों का तारा. Model answer: समय पर न पढ़ने वाले विद्यार्थी अंत में हाथ मलते रह जाते हैं। मोहन अपने दादाजी की आँखों का तारा है। [Students who do not study on time are left regretting. Mohan is the apple of his grandfather's eye.]

Step 1, Plan a comparison. Choose two seasons, here summer and winter, and list points to compare: temperature, rain, activities, feeling. Then write a topic sentence: الصَّيْفُ وَالشِّتَاءُ فَصْلَانِ مُخْتَلِفَانِ. [Summer and winter are two different seasons.]

Step 2, Use the comparative adjective أَفْعَلُ مِنْ. الصَّيْفُ أَكْثَرُ حَرَارَةً مِنَ الشِّتَاءِ. [Summer is hotter than winter.] الشِّتَاءُ أَبْرَدُ وَأَكْثَرُ مَطَرًا. [Winter is colder and rainier.] The word مِنْ introduces the thing compared.

Step 3, Contrast with linking words. بَيْنَمَا الشِّتَاءُ بَارِدٌ، فَإِنَّ الصَّيْفَ حَارٌّ. [While winter is cold, summer is hot.] فِي الصَّيْفِ نَسْبَحُ فِي الْبَحْرِ، أَمَّا فِي الشِّتَاءِ فَنَجْلِسُ قُرْبَ الْمِدْفَأَةِ. [In summer we swim in the sea, whereas in winter we sit by the heater.]

Step 4, Conclude with your preference. أُفَضِّلُ الشِّتَاءَ لِأَنَّ الْجَوَّ هَادِئٌ وَأُحِبُّ صَوْتَ الْمَطَرِ. [I prefer winter because the weather is calm and I love the sound of rain.] Read all four sentences together and check each has a clear link.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes الصَّيْفُ أَكْثَرُ حَرَارَةً الشِّتَاءِ. Correction: add مِنَ: الصَّيْفُ أَكْثَرُ حَرَارَةً مِنَ الشِّتَاءِ. Another says الصَّيْفُ حَارٌّ وَالشِّتَاءُ بَارِدٌ only; that lists, not compares. Use أَكْثَرُ and مِنْ.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences comparing spring and autumn. Model answer: الرَّبِيعُ أَجْمَلُ مِنَ الْخَرِيفِ لِأَنَّ الْأَزْهَارَ تَتَفَتَّحُ. بَيْنَمَا يَكُونُ الْخَرِيفُ أَهْدَأَ. أُفَضِّلُ الرَّبِيعَ. [Spring is more beautiful than autumn because flowers open. While autumn is calmer. I prefer spring.]

Step 1, Name community words. الْجَارُ [neighbour], الْحَيُّ [neighbourhood], التَّعَاوُنُ [cooperation], الْمُسَاعَدَةُ [help], الْمَرِيضُ [the sick person], الْمُسِنُّ [the elderly]. Use them in a mind map around the word الْمُجْتَمَعُ [society].

Step 2, Describe your neighbourhood. يَسْكُنُ بِجَوَارِنَا جَارٌ طَيِّبٌ. [A kind neighbour lives next to us.] يَتَعَاوَنُ أَهْلُ الْحَيِّ فِي تَنْظِيفِ الشَّارِعِ. [The people of the neighbourhood cooperate in cleaning the street.] نَزُورُ الْمَرِيضَ وَنُسَاعِدُ الْمُسِنَّ. [We visit the sick and help the elderly.]

Step 3, Use relative clauses. الْجَارُ الَّذِي يُسَاعِدُنَا طَيِّبٌ. [The neighbour who helps us is kind.] The relative pronoun الَّذِي is used after a definite noun. After an indefinite noun leave it out: جَارٌ يُسَاعِدُنَا [a neighbour who helps us].

Step 4, Write a paragraph. الْحَيُّ الَّذِي أَسْكُنُ فِيهِ هَادِئٌ. يَجْتَمِعُ الْجِيرَانُ فِي الْأَعْيَادِ وَيَتَبَادَلُونَ الْحَلْوَى. لِذَلِكَ نَشْعُرُ بِالْأَمَانِ وَالْمَحَبَّةِ. [The neighbourhood I live in is quiet. Neighbours gather at festivals and exchange sweets. So we feel safe and loved.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes جَارٌ الَّذِي يُسَاعِدُنَا. Correction: جَارٌ يُسَاعِدُنَا without الَّذِي, because جَارٌ is indefinite; or الْجَارُ الَّذِي يُسَاعِدُنَا with a definite noun. Also match the pronoun: الَّتِي for a feminine noun.

Step 6, Your turn: write a short paragraph about how your neighbourhood helps people. Model answer: فِي حَيِّنَا جِيرَانٌ يَتَعَاوَنُونَ. الْمَرْأَةُ الَّتِي تَسْكُنُ بِجَانِبِنَا تُسَاعِدُ الْمُسِنِّينَ. هَكَذَا يَكُونُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ قَوِيًّا. [In our neighbourhood neighbours cooperate. The woman who lives next to us helps the elderly. This is how society becomes strong.]

Step 1, A nominal sentence (جُمْلَةٌ اسْمِيَّةٌ) begins with a noun: الْوَلَدُ مُجْتَهِدٌ. [The boy is hardworking.] It has a subject (مُبْتَدَأٌ) الْوَلَدُ and a predicate (خَبَرٌ) مُجْتَهِدٌ, both in the nominative.

Step 2, A verbal sentence (جُمْلَةٌ فِعْلِيَّةٌ) begins with a verb: يَكْتُبُ الطَّالِبُ الدَّرْسَ. [The student writes the lesson.] Parts: verb يَكْتُبُ, doer (فَاعِلٌ) الطَّالِبُ in the nominative, object (مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ) الدَّرْسَ in the accusative.

Step 3, Compare the order. الطَّالِبُ يَكْتُبُ الدَّرْسَ is a nominal sentence, because it begins with a noun; its predicate is the verbal phrase يَكْتُبُ الدَّرْسَ. Both mean the same, but the grammar name depends on the first word.

Step 4, After إِنَّ the subject becomes accusative. إِنَّ الطَّالِبَ مُجْتَهِدٌ. [Indeed the student is hardworking.] Contrast with the plain sentence الطَّالِبُ مُجْتَهِدٌ. Now analyse: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً. [The boy wrote a letter.] Verb كَتَبَ, doer الْوَلَدُ, object رِسَالَةً.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student calls الطَّالِبُ يَكْتُبُ a verbal sentence. Correction: it begins with a noun, so it is nominal. Another writes كَتَبَ الْوَلَدَ رِسَالَةً with a fatha on الْوَلَدَ; the doer takes damma: كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ رِسَالَةً.

Step 6, Your turn: analyse يَقْرَأُ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ and write one nominal sentence. Model answer: verbal; verb يَقْرَأُ, doer الْوَلَدُ, object الْكِتَابَ. Nominal: الْكِتَابُ مُفِيدٌ. [The book is useful.] Subject and predicate are both nominative.

Step 1, An essay has three parts: introduction (مُقَدِّمَةٌ), body (عَرْضٌ), conclusion (خَاتِمَةٌ). Topic: the importance of reading. Open with a general claim: الْقِرَاءَةُ غِذَاءُ الْعَقْلِ، وَهِيَ مِفْتَاحُ الْمَعْرِفَةِ. [Reading is food for the mind and the key to knowledge.]

Step 2, Write the first body paragraph. أَوَّلًا، تُوَسِّعُ الْقِرَاءَةُ مَعْلُومَاتِنَا. فَالْكِتَابُ يَأْخُذُنَا إِلَى بِلَادٍ لَمْ نَزُرْهَا. [First, reading widens our knowledge. A book takes us to countries we have not visited.] Give a claim, then an explanation.

Step 3, Write the second paragraph. ثَانِيًا، تُحَسِّنُ الْقِرَاءَةُ لُغَتَنَا وَتُنَمِّي خَيَالَنَا. فَمَنْ يَقْرَأُ كَثِيرًا يَكْتُبُ بِأُسْلُوبٍ أَجْمَلَ. [Second, reading improves our language and develops our imagination. Whoever reads a lot writes in a nicer style.]

Step 4, Conclude. لِذَلِكَ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَجْعَلَ الْقِرَاءَةَ عَادَةً يَوْمِيَّةً. [Therefore we must make reading a daily habit.] A conclusion restates the claim in different words and ends with advice. Never introduce a new argument here.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes one block with no introduction and repeats the same point three times. Correction: divide into introduction, two body paragraphs with different arguments, and a conclusion, and link them with أَوَّلًا، ثَانِيًا، لِذَلِكَ.

Step 6, Your turn: outline and write an introduction for the essay The value of time. Model answer: الْوَقْتُ أَثْمَنُ مَا نَمْلِكُ، وَمَنْ أَحْسَنَ اسْتِعْمَالَهُ نَجَحَ. [Time is the most precious thing we own, and whoever uses it well succeeds.] Outline: 1 planning, 2 avoiding waste, 3 result.

Step 1, The near future uses aller plus the infinitive. Je vais partir demain. [I am going to leave tomorrow.] Nous allons visiter le musée. [We are going to visit the museum.] Conjugate aller correctly: je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont.

Step 2, The recent past uses venir de plus the infinitive. Je viens de manger. [I have just eaten.] Elle vient d'arriver. [She has just arrived.] Conjugate venir: je viens, tu viens, il vient, nous venons, vous venez, ils viennent.

Step 3, The present continuous uses être en train de plus the infinitive. Je suis en train de lire. [I am in the middle of reading.] Ils sont en train de jouer. [They are playing right now.] It stresses that the action is happening at this moment.

Step 4, Dialogue. Maman : Tu viens de finir tes devoirs ? [Have you just finished your homework?] Léo : Non, je suis en train de les faire. [No, I am doing them.] Maman : Et après ? [And afterwards?] Léo : Après, je vais jouer au foot. [Afterwards I am going to play football.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says je viens de mangé. Correction: je viens de manger, with the infinitive. Another says je vais de partir. Correction: je vais partir, with no de. A third says je suis en train lire; correction: je suis en train de lire.

Step 6, Your turn: write one sentence with each form about a trip. Model answer: Nous allons partir à la mer. Je viens de préparer ma valise. Maman est en train de réserver les billets. [We are going to leave for the sea. I have just packed my case. Mum is in the middle of booking the tickets.]

Step 1, The pronoun y replaces à plus a place or thing. Tu vas à Paris ? Oui, j'y vais. [Are you going to Paris? Yes, I am going there.] Il pense à son voyage. Il y pense. [He thinks about his trip. He thinks about it.] Y goes before the verb.

Step 2, The pronoun en replaces de plus a noun or a quantity. Tu veux du pain ? Oui, j'en veux. [Do you want some bread? Yes, I want some.] Elle vient de Lyon. Elle en vient. [She comes from Lyon. She comes from there.] J'ai deux frères. J'en ai deux. [I have two brothers. I have two.]

Step 3, Position rules. With the near future the pronoun goes before the infinitive: Je vais y aller. [I am going to go there.] In the negative: Je n'y vais pas. Je n'en veux pas. [I am not going there. I do not want any.] The pronoun stays next to its verb.

Step 4, Dialogue. Paul : Tu es allé au cinéma ? [Did you go to the cinema?] Zoé : Oui, j'y suis allée hier. [Yes, I went there yesterday.] Paul : Tu as pris des chips ? [Did you get some crisps?] Zoé : Oui, j'en ai pris. [Yes, I got some.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says Je en veux. Correction: J'en veux, with elision. Another says J'en ai deux frères. Correction: J'en ai deux, because en already replaces frères. A third says Je vais à y aller; correction: Je vais y aller.

Step 6, Your turn: rewrite with y or en. Elle va à l'école. Nous avons trois chats. Je ne veux pas de lait. Model answer: Elle y va. Nous en avons trois. Je n'en veux pas. [She goes there. We have three. I do not want any.]

Step 1, Read my travel passage. सुबह जब हमारी ट्रेन हिमालय की तलहटी में पहुँची, तो ठंडी हवा ने हमारा स्वागत किया। खिड़की के बाहर देवदार के ऊँचे पेड़ और बादलों में छिपी चोटियाँ दिखाई दे रही थीं। [When our train reached the Himalayan foothills, cold air welcomed us. Outside, tall deodar trees and cloud-hidden peaks were visible.]

Step 2, Read the end. एक छोटे-से ढाबे पर हमने गरम चाय पी और स्थानीय लोगों से बातें कीं। उस दिन मुझे लगा कि यात्रा केवल जगह बदलना नहीं, नज़रिया बदलना भी है। [At a small eatery we drank hot tea and chatted with locals. I felt that travel also changes one's outlook.]

Step 3, Notice the features of travel writing (यात्रा-वृत्तांत): first person (हमारी, मुझे), description of sights and weather, small events, and a closing thought. Find an example of each in the passage and mark it with a different colour.

Step 4, Write a summary. लेखक की ट्रेन हिमालय की तलहटी में पहुँची। उन्होंने पेड़ और चोटियाँ देखीं, चाय पी और स्थानीय लोगों से बात की। उन्होंने सीखा कि यात्रा दृष्टिकोण भी बदलती है। [The writer's train reached the Himalayan foothills. They saw trees and peaks, drank tea and spoke with locals. They learned that travel changes viewpoint.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student copies every description of scenery into the summary. Correction: keep only main events and the final thought; the summary should be about a third of the length, in your own words, without your opinion.

Step 6, Your turn: answer what the writer felt at the end. Model answer: लेखक को लगा कि यात्रा केवल नई जगह देखना नहीं है, बल्कि सोचने का तरीका बदलना भी है। [The writer felt that travel is not only seeing a new place but also changing the way one thinks.]

Step 1, Read the couplet I wrote in devotional style. सच्चा मन ही मंदिर है, सेवा ही है पूजा। जो दुखियों के आँसू पोंछे, उससे बड़ा न दूजा। [A sincere heart is the temple, and service is worship. One who wipes the tears of the suffering has no equal.]
Step 2, Understand the words. मंदिर [temple], सेवा [service], पूजा [worship], दुखी [suffering], आँसू [tears], पोंछना [to wipe], दूजा [another]. Note the rhyme: पूजा and दूजा end in the same sound.

Step 3, Explain the meaning. The poet says that worship is not only ritual but kindness. The heart is a temple, so goodness inside matters most. Write: कवि के अनुसार सच्ची भक्ति दूसरों की सेवा में है। [According to the poet, true devotion lies in serving others.]

Step 4, Name the style. Devotional poems (भक्ति काव्य) praise goodness and ask the reader to live well. Classical couplets state a truth in two lines with a clear image, such as आँसू पोंछना. Read aloud, pausing at the comma, then at the end of each line.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student says the poem teaches only to go to the temple. Correction: it says the heart is the temple, so the teaching is service and kindness. Always explain the idea, not just the words.

Step 6, Your turn: explain the second line in your own words. Model answer: जो व्यक्ति दुखी लोगों की सहायता करता है, वही सबसे महान है। [The person who helps the suffering is the greatest.] This keeps the poet's meaning.

Step 1, Sentences by meaning. विधानवाचक: राम पढ़ता है। [statement] निषेधवाचक: राम नहीं पढ़ता। [negative] प्रश्नवाचक: क्या राम पढ़ता है? [question] आज्ञावाचक: बैठ जाओ। [command] विस्मयादिबोधक: वाह! कितना सुंदर! [exclamation] इच्छावाचक: ईश्वर करे तुम सफल हो। [wish].

Step 2, Sentences by structure. सरल: राम पढ़ता है। [simple: one verb] संयुक्त: राम पढ़ता है और श्याम खेलता है। [compound: two equal clauses] मिश्र: जो मेहनत करता है, वह सफल होता है। [complex: a main and a dependent clause].

Step 3, Vocabulary types. तत्सम words come straight from Sanskrit: सूर्य [sun]. तद्भव words come from them but changed: सूरज. Others: अग्नि–आग, रात्रि–रात. Use each in a sentence: सूर्य पूर्व में उगता है। [The sun rises in the east.]

Step 4, Identify types in a paragraph. क्या तुम कल आओगे? (प्रश्नवाचक) हाँ, मैं आऊँगा। (विधानवाचक) देर मत करना। (निषेध or आज्ञा) वाह, कितना अच्छा मौसम! (विस्मय) Say the type of each sentence and what clue tells you.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student labels क्या तुम आओगे? as आज्ञावाचक. Correction: it is प्रश्नवाचक because it asks a question. Another calls राम पढ़ता है और श्याम खेलता है a simple sentence; it has two clauses, so it is compound.

Step 6, Your turn: write one question and one complex sentence. Model answer: क्या तुमने गृहकार्य कर लिया? जब बारिश होती है, तब किसान खुश हो जाते हैं। [Have you done your homework? When it rains, farmers become happy.] The second has a dependent clause.

Step 1, Read the unseen passage. पानी हमारे जीवन का आधार है, फिर भी हम इसे बेदर्दी से बहाते हैं। एक नल से टपकती हर बूँद दिन भर में कई लीटर पानी बर्बाद कर देती है। [Water is the basis of life, yet we waste it carelessly. Each dripping drop from a tap wastes many litres a day.]

Step 2, Read the rest. वर्षा का जल एकत्र करके हम इसे बगीचे और सफ़ाई में उपयोग कर सकते हैं। यदि हर परिवार थोड़ी-सी सावधानी बरते, तो आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए पानी बचा रहेगा। [By collecting rainwater we can use it for gardens and cleaning. If every family takes a little care, water will remain for coming generations.]

Step 3, Answer literal questions in full sentences. हम वर्षा के जल का क्या उपयोग कर सकते हैं? [How can we use rainwater?] हम वर्षा के जल को एकत्र करके बगीचे और सफ़ाई में उपयोग कर सकते हैं। [By collecting it we can use it for gardens and cleaning.]

Step 4, Answer vocabulary, inference and title. आधार का अर्थ है सहारा। [आधार means support.] नल की टपकती बूँद क्यों हानिकारक है? क्योंकि वह दिन भर में बहुत पानी बर्बाद करती है। [A dripping tap harms because it wastes much water.] Title: जल बचाओ.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student answers क्यों हानिकारक है? with बहुत पानी, which is incomplete. Correction: write a full answer starting from the question words: टपकती बूँद इसलिए हानिकारक है क्योंकि वह दिन भर में कई लीटर पानी बर्बाद कर देती है।

Step 6, Your turn: answer what happens if every family takes care. Model answer: यदि हर परिवार थोड़ी-सी सावधानी बरतेगा, तो आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए पानी बचा रहेगा। [If every family takes a little care, water will remain for future generations.]

Step 1, Read the short text I wrote. أَنَا النَّخْلَةُ، جُذُورِي فِي التُّرَابِ وَرَأْسِي فِي السَّمَاءِ. تَهُزُّنِي الرِّيحُ فَلَا أَسْقُطُ، وَأُعْطِي التَّمْرَ لِمَنْ يَمُرُّ بِي. [I am the palm tree, my roots in the soil and my head in the sky. The wind shakes me but I do not fall, and I give dates to whoever passes by.]

Step 2, Identify the theme. The palm stands for a person who is steadfast and generous. Write: يَرْمُزُ النَّصُّ بِالنَّخْلَةِ إِلَى الْإِنْسَانِ الصَّبُورِ الْكَرِيمِ. [The text uses the palm to symbolise the patient, generous person.] Support it with a quotation.

Step 3, Name the devices. تَشْخِيصٌ [personification]: the palm speaks as أَنَا. طِبَاقٌ [antithesis]: التُّرَابِ and السَّمَاءِ, the low and the high. اسْتِعَارَةٌ [metaphor]: the palm as the human being. Each device adds to the meaning.

Step 4, Write an analysis paragraph. يُبْرِزُ الْكَاتِبُ ثَبَاتَ الْإِنْسَانِ مِنْ خِلَالِ عِبَارَةِ «جُذُورِي فِي التُّرَابِ وَرَأْسِي فِي السَّمَاءِ»، فَالطِّبَاقُ يُصَوِّرُ التَّوَاضُعَ مَعَ الطُّمُوحِ. [The writer highlights steadfastness through the phrase, roots in the soil and head in the sky; the contrast depicts humility with ambition.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student only paraphrases: النَّخْلَةُ لَهَا جُذُورٌ وَتُعْطِي التَّمْرَ. Correction: analysis explains how and why: name the device, quote the words, and say what effect they create, such as showing generosity and strength.

Step 6, Your turn: analyse the line تَهُزُّنِي الرِّيحُ فَلَا أَسْقُطُ. Model answer: تَدُلُّ الْجُمْلَةُ عَلَى الْمُثَابَرَةِ؛ فَالرِّيحُ رَمْزٌ لِلصُّعُوبَاتِ، وَالنَّخْلَةُ لَا تَسْقُطُ كَالْإِنْسَانِ الصَّبُورِ. [The sentence shows perseverance; the wind symbolises difficulties, and the palm does not fall, like a patient person.]

Step 1, A formal letter has a date, the addressee, a formal greeting, a body, a closing and a signature. Address: حَضْرَةِ الْأُسْتَاذِ مُدِيرِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ الْمُحْتَرَمِ. [To the respected school principal.] Greeting: تَحِيَّةً طَيِّبَةً وَبَعْدُ، [With best greetings, and then,].

Step 2, Write the opening of the body. أَتَقَدَّمُ إِلَيْكُمْ بِطَلَبٍ لِإِقَامَةِ مَعْرِضٍ لِلْكِتَابِ فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ الْقَادِمِ. [I submit to you a request to hold a book fair at school next Thursday.] State the request in the first sentence.

Step 3, Give reasons and details. يَهْدِفُ الْمَعْرِضُ إِلَى تَشْجِيعِ الطُّلَّابِ عَلَى الْقِرَاءَةِ، وَسَيُشَارِكُ فِيهِ أَوْلِيَاءُ الْأُمُورِ. لِذَا أَرْجُو التَّكَرُّمَ بِالْمُوَافَقَةِ. [The fair aims to encourage students to read, and parents will take part. I therefore ask you kindly to approve.]

Step 4, Close and sign. وَتَفَضَّلُوا بِقَبُولِ فَائِقِ الِاحْتِرَامِ وَالتَّقْدِيرِ. [Please accept my highest respect and appreciation.] مُقَدِّمُ الطَّلَبِ: خَالِدٌ، الصَّفُّ الْعَاشِرُ. [Applicant: Khalid, grade ten.] Keep the language polite and the sentences short.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student starts the letter with مَرْحَبًا يَا مُدِيرُ [Hello, principal], uses slang, and forgets the date. Correction: open with the formal address, تَحِيَّةً طَيِّبَةً وَبَعْدُ، write standard Arabic, and put the date at the top.

Step 6, Your turn: write the body of a letter asking permission to organise a charity day. Model answer: أَتَقَدَّمُ إِلَيْكُمْ بِطَلَبٍ لِتَنْظِيمِ يَوْمٍ خَيْرِيٍّ لِجَمْعِ التَّبَرُّعَاتِ. أَرْجُو التَّكَرُّمَ بِالْمُوَافَقَةِ. وَتَفَضَّلُوا بِقَبُولِ الِاحْتِرَامِ. [I request permission to organise a charity day to collect donations. I kindly ask for approval. Please accept my respect.]

Step 1, Listen to this announcement, which a partner reads once. تُعْلِنُ إِدَارَةُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ عَنْ إِقَامَةِ يَوْمٍ لِلنَّظَافَةِ يَوْمَ الْأَحَدِ الْقَادِمِ، وَسَيُشَارِكُ فِيهِ ثَلَاثُمِائَةِ طَالِبٍ. [The school administration announces a cleaning day next Sunday, with three hundred students taking part.]

Step 2, Hear the second half. سَيَبْدَأُ الْعَمَلُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ صَبَاحًا وَيَنْتَهِي عِنْدَ الظُّهْرِ. عَلَى كُلِّ طَالِبٍ إِحْضَارُ قُفَّازَاتٍ وَكِيسٍ. [Work will start at nine in the morning and finish at noon. Each student must bring gloves and a bag.]

Step 3, Take notes while listening. Write key words only: يَوْمُ نَظَافَةٍ، الْأَحَدُ، 300 طَالِبٍ، 9 صَبَاحًا – ظُهْرًا، قُفَّازَاتٌ وَكِيسٌ. [cleaning day, Sunday, 300 students, 9 am to noon, gloves and bag.] Notes use words and numbers, not full sentences.

Step 4, Write the summary from your notes. أَعْلَنَتِ الْمَدْرَسَةُ عَنْ يَوْمِ نَظَافَةٍ يَوْمَ الْأَحَدِ، يُشَارِكُ فِيهِ ثَلَاثُمِائَةِ طَالِبٍ مِنَ التَّاسِعَةِ حَتَّى الظُّهْرِ، وَعَلَى كُلِّ طَالِبٍ إِحْضَارُ قُفَّازَاتٍ وَكِيسٍ. [The school announced a cleaning day on Sunday with three hundred students from nine until noon; each must bring gloves and a bag.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student tries to write every word and loses the numbers and times. Correction: note who, what, when, how many and what to bring; leave out repeated words and add linking words only when writing the summary.

Step 6, Your turn: summarise a different announcement about a trip next Friday at eight, with fifty students, bringing lunch. Model answer: سَتَنْظِمُ الْمَدْرَسَةُ رِحْلَةً يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ الْقَادِمِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّامِنَةِ، وَيُشَارِكُ فِيهَا خَمْسُونَ طَالِبًا، وَعَلَى كُلِّ طَالِبٍ إِحْضَارُ غَدَاءٍ. [The school will organise a trip next Friday at eight, with fifty students; each must bring lunch.]

Step 1, Open with a hook and a thesis. هَلْ فَكَّرْتُمْ يَوْمًا كَمْ لِتْرًا مِنَ الْمَاءِ نُهْدِرُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ؟ [Have you ever thought how many litres of water we waste each day?] مَوْضُوعِي الْيَوْمَ هُوَ أَهَمِّيَّةُ الْحِفَاظِ عَلَى الْمَاءِ. [My topic today is the importance of saving water.]

Step 2, Present the structure aloud. سَأَتَحَدَّثُ عَنْ ثَلَاثَةِ أُمُورٍ: أَوَّلًا أَسْبَابُ الْهَدْرِ، ثَانِيًا آثَارُهُ، وَثَالِثًا الْحُلُولُ. [I will talk about three things: first the causes of waste, second its effects, and third solutions.] Signposting helps listeners follow.

Step 3, Develop each point with an example. أَوَّلًا، يُهْدِرُ بَعْضُنَا الْمَاءَ حِينَ يُغْلِقُ الصُّنْبُورَ بِإِهْمَالٍ. [First, some of us waste water by closing the tap carelessly.] ثَانِيًا، يُؤَدِّي ذَلِكَ إِلَى نَقْصِ الْمَاءِ لِلْأَجْيَالِ الْقَادِمَةِ. [Second, this leads to a shortage for coming generations.]

Step 4, Give solutions and close. ثَالِثًا، يُمْكِنُنَا جَمْعُ مِيَاهِ الْأَمْطَارِ وَإِصْلَاحُ التَّسْرِيبِ. وَفِي الْخِتَامِ أَدْعُوكُمْ لِلْبَدْءِ الْيَوْمَ. شُكْرًا لِحُسْنِ اسْتِمَاعِكُمْ. [Third, we can collect rainwater and fix leaks. In conclusion I call on you to begin today. Thank you for your attention.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A speaker reads from the slides without looking up and gives no example. Correction: use only key words on the slides, speak to the audience, pause after each point, and add one example. Respond to questions with سُؤَالٌ وَجِيهٌ [a good question] before answering.

Step 6, Your turn: write a thirty-second introduction and thesis on screen time. Model answer: هَلْ تَعْرِفُونَ كَمْ سَاعَةً نَقْضِيهَا أَمَامَ الشَّاشَةِ؟ مَوْضُوعِي الْيَوْمَ أَثَرُ الْإِفْرَاطِ فِي اسْتِعْمَالِ الشَّاشَاتِ عَلَى صِحَّتِنَا. [Do you know how many hours we spend in front of the screen? My topic today is the effect of excessive screen use on our health.]
